### F-172: the UI containers are never inflated because the guest's own inflate loop is entered with a **byte count of 0** - every `XMem`/`INFLATE-ENTER` line at this frontier is our re-point machinery feeding it a bounce buffer whose address is a **semaphore handle**, so "the RSC5 payload will not decode" was never actually tested (read-site window hypothesis REFUTED, code reverted)

- Task:    B5 (menu) / B4's feed - the codec question F-170/F-171 left open; answers it
- Type:    FACT (root cause) + INFERENCE (what to fix) + a recorded refutation of my own prior hypothesis
- Class:   G (the game's coded behaviour) with a D/E component (what our device returns)
- Priority: P0 - it is the single blocker on the UI route, and it says the blocker is ours to remove, not a cipher
- Evidence: `build/w182.log` (new soak, binary `3584fca` + one reverted edit) lines 3972/3985/3990 and the `READWRAP`/`INFLATE-ENTER` pair; `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.14.cpp:19040-19140` (`sub_821BC140`'s priming block and its `bl InflateBegin`); `ppc_recomp.18.cpp:10831`-ff (`sub_821D5E10` = `zlibInflater::InflateBegin`, register-accurate); `build/cache/mcla_pe.bin` strings `0x82015770`/`0x820157AC`/`0x820157D4`; `src/gpu_device.cpp:7067`-ff (the hook) and `:3646`-ff (its own comment)

**What the guest's own code requires, read off the generated listing.** `sub_821BC140` is the only
caller of `zlibInflater::InflateBegin` (`tools/ppc_xrefs.py calls 0x821D5E10` -> one site,
`0x821BC37C`). Its loop does:

```
r30 = [r28 + 4]                     // the byte count still to inflate
r31 = min(r30, 32768)               // 0x821BC2D4-0x821BC2DC: cmplwi r30,32768 / mr r31,r30
r3 = [r28+8] -> [[r3]+28](r3, r20, cursor@(r1+80), dst = r1+128, r7 = r31)   // device Read
if ([r27+1852] == 0 && r3 == r31) {          // ONLY on an exactly-full read
    [r1+96] = r3 - r29                        // inflater st+0  (remaining INPUT)
    [r1+100] = (r1+128) + r29                 // inflater st+4  (input pointer)
    cursor += r3
}
InflateBegin(r3 = r24, r4 = r1 + 96)          // the state is a STACK object
```
`InflateBegin` then requires `st+8 == 0`, compares `*st+4` against **`0x0FF512EF`**
(`lis r10,0FF5` + `ori r9,r10,12EF`, `ppc_recomp.18.cpp:10865`-ff) - failing that it prints
`zlibInflater::InflateBegin - not in XCompress format` - consumes 8 bytes (magic + size at src+4)
and calls `sub_8244FF20` = **XMemDecompress** (`XMemCreateDecompressionContext`, same string block).
So the RSC5 header's `+0x0C` magic / `+0x10` size pair is the XCompress sub-header, and the LZX
stream starts at **`pkg+0x14`**. The magic occurs exactly once per package in the archive, always at
`pkg+0x0C` (measured over each package's whole declared range), which confirms the framing.

**Why it never runs.** `READWRAP sub_821CC6F0 #1 ... r5=00060000 r6=006D8F40 r7=0 ... ret=00000000
lr=821BC334` - the read that feeds the inflate is asked for **`r7 = 0` bytes** (`r7` is the count,
`r6` the caller's stack destination), because `[r28+4]` is 0. An exactly-full read of zero still
satisfies `r3 == r31`, so the guest primes the stack state anyway and computes
`st+0 = 0 - 12 = 0xFFFFFFF4` and `st+4 = (r1+128) + 12 = 0x006D8F4C` - **which is exactly what
`INFLATE-ENTER #1 st=006D8F20 in=4294967284 inPtr=006D8F4C consumed=0` prints** (st = r1+96, and
`r1 = 006D8EC0` is visible in the same log as `r1in=`). Two independent derivations agreeing to the
dword: the count is 0 before we ever touch it.

**What our code then does with it.** `PPC_FUNC(sub_821D5E10)` (`src/gpu_device.cpp:7067`-ff)
re-points `st+0`/`st+4` at a host bounce whenever the magic is absent (its own comment at
`:3646`-ff calls this a short-circuit), and the resulting XMem calls are ours, with our constants:
every one of the 34 `XMEM` lines carries `srcSz=7179936 destSz=7179940`, the hard-coded
`j1SrcSz`/`j1DestSz` at `src/gpu_device.cpp:4322`-`4323`, and `ret=00000000`. The `src=` of the first
is `CA327114` - **`CA327100` is a semaphore** (`SEMA-CREATE #31 h=CA327100 init=0 max=32767`,
`PRELOAD-CTX #1 ... arcDev=CA327100`), so we are handing the guest's LZX decoder a kernel object's
memory and reading "XMem produced nothing" as a property of the archive. It is not.
**Consequence, stated plainly: F-091/F-102's "the only inflate door was reached and produced 0" and
F-170's "the payload is encrypted or an unimplemented codec" are both unsupported - the door was
never fed real bytes.**

**My own prior hypothesis, refuted in the same soak.** I changed the `sub_821CC6F0` read site to
(a) prefer the record's own validated package over the path-substring map (F-171's recorded open
item) and (b) size the bounce by the declared length. `w182` is **identical to `w181` on every

### F-173: the zero inflate count has a single, named source - `sub_82187150` is the ONLY caller of the streamer's request registrar and it calls it with a zero scalar twice per boot; `REQFILL` proves it with a census whose frontier delta is exactly zero

**Addendum to F-175, same session (2026-09-24 ~17:30) - stated precisely, because the headline above
over-reaches.** Reading the rest of `pgStreamer::Open`'s body
(`ppc_recomp.14.cpp`, the span after the `InitClass` assert): it does **not** demonstrably write the
consumer's array. What it actually does is

```
lwz  r11,0(r24)          // r24 = 0x8283D1A4  -> loads [0x8283D1A4], NOT [0x8283D1C4]
mulli r10,r10,28
add  r29,r10,r11         // r29 = a 28-byte record in the array based at [0x8283D1A4]
stw  r25,16(r29)         // r25 = 0
...  helper calls at 0x823DD800 / 0x823DD7F0 / 0x823DD850 on r30 (= its name-ish arg,
     and on r30+6, and with a length cap of 44) - CRT-region addresses, name/string work
stw  r25,8(r29); stw r25,20(r29); stw r11,4(r29)   // r11 = (helper result) + r31
```
So the correct statements are: (a) `Open` computes the **address** `0x8283D1C4` (which is the field
`sub_821BC140` reads its array base from) and separately indexes a 28-byte array through the
*neighbouring* field `0x8283D1A4` - the two are 0x30 apart in the same `pgStreamer` class static;
(b) the value it puts in `[record+4]` is built from string helpers applied to its argument, which is
**not** the shape of a byte count; and (c) therefore `Open` is a strong candidate for the *owner and
initialiser* of the handle arrays (consistent with the `pgStreamer::InitClass` assert and the
`out of handles` message), but it is **not** established as the writer of the specific field the
inflate loop consumes.

Why the field is nevertheless certainly a count *at the consumer*: `sub_821BC140` loads
`r30 = [r28+4]` (`ppc_recomp.14.cpp:18967`), clamps it (`cmplwi r30,32768`), and passes the clamp as
the device Read's count argument (`r7 = r31`, indirect call at `0x821BC334`) - and **no write to `r28`
occurs between `:18873` (where it is formed) and `:19052`**, re-checked over that whole span, not just
part of it. The measured consequence in `w182` is the 0-byte read with `lr=821BC334`, so the field's
*role* is proven by the log even while its *writer* is still unnamed.

Corrected next step, still static and still one address wide: find what stores into
`[0x8283D1C4]` (the array-base field) and what writes `[record+4]` in **that** array - i.e. trace the
users of the base rather than assuming `Open` is one. `xref 0x8283D1C4` gives the single computation
site above, so the search is for stores through pointers derived from it, which means reading
`sub_821BC674`-`sub_821BC694` (the three reads of the class static that sit inside the same function
family as the inflate loop) and `sub_821BCB10+0x44` (our `ENQ` chooser). If neither writes it, the
array is filled by `pgStreamer::InitClass` sizing plus a per-request insert elsewhere, and a
registers-only census at `sub_821BC140`'s *caller* (`sub_821BC910`, the enqueue path that produced
`INLINE-EXEC #n`) is the cheapest admissible way to see the request as it is handed over.

### F-176: the handle id that selects the zero-length record is the value `sub_821867A0` returned - `REQFILL #2 -> r3=00000004` and `ENQ a0=00000004` / `REQDUMP d[0]=00000004` are the same number, so F-173's builder and F-172's zero are now joined by a measured identity, not by an inferred field path

- Task:    B5 (menu) - continues F-174/F-175's static trace and fixes what is and is not known
- Type:    FACT (three-way log identity) + FACT (listing-derived structure) + an explicit open question
- Class:   G
- Priority: P1
- Evidence: `build/w183.log`: `REQFILL sub_821867A0 #2 … -> r3=00000004`, `ENQ sub_821BCB10 #1 a0=00000004 cb=821BC548 -> r3=82849B2C`, `REQDUMP #1 a0=82849B2C d=[00000004 …]`, `INLINE-EXEC sub_821BC140 #1 a0=82849B2C`; `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.14.cpp` (`sub_821BC910` body, `sub_821BCB10` prologue, `sub_821BC140+0x24`)

**The queue record is 1556 bytes, confirmed from the listing.** `sub_821BC910` computes
`r31 = instance*24948 + <static base>`, then `r30 = r31 + ([r31+24932] * 1556)`, and calls
`sub_821BC140(r3 = r30, r4 = instance)` **only when `[r30+1548] != 0`**. So the request the inflate
loop executes is a 1556-byte (0x614) queue slot - which is what Session 75n's `REQDUMP` comment
asserted from the other direction, and it is why `d[0]` of that dump is the value `sub_821BC140`
multiplies by 28. The ring head at `[r31+24932]` wraps at **16** (`cmpwi r11,16`), so this queue holds
sixteen outstanding requests, and the three `INLINE-EXEC` firings correspond to three `ENQ` firings
whose `a0` values are `4`, `0x8004`, `0x10004`.

**The identity.** `sub_821BCB10` (`ENQ`, registers-only, 3 firings) takes those values as its first
argument and returns the queue object; `sub_821BC140` then uses the same low half (`4`) as its
handle index; and `REQFILL` records that `sub_821867A0`'s **second** call returned exactly
`r3 = 00000004`. So the number that selects the record whose `[+4]` is 0 is the number that
`sub_821867A0` handed back. That is a measured three-way match across `REQFILL` / `ENQ` / `REQDUMP`,
not an inferred field path, and it is the strongest link so far between the builder and the zero.

**What is still NOT known, stated so nobody over-reads this.** `sub_821BCB10` only *searches* the
`[0x8283D1C4]`-based 28-byte array (`mulli r11,r30,28` / `lwzx r9,r11,r26` / compare against
`record+0`), and `sub_821867A0` writes the record array it is *handed* (F-174). Whether the builder's
local record is then copied into the global pool - which the matching id would suggest - is not
established, and neither is the store that would put a **length** rather than the string-derived value
seen in `pgStreamer::Open` into `[global record+4]`. The two candidate next reads, both static:
(a) the tail of `sub_821867A0` after its four `[entry+4]` stores, looking for a copy loop into a
pool whose base comes from `[0x8283D1C4]`; (b) `sub_821BC674`-`0x821BC694`, the three reads of the
same class static inside the inflate family, which are the most likely completion path that would
*advance* a record's `[+4]` as bytes are consumed.

### F-177: the zero inflate length is produced by a **vtable slot we never implemented** - `pgStreamer::Open` sets `record.length := obj->vtable[+84](obj)`, and slot +84 of the `memory:` device is the shared stub `0x821A5CC0` that 13 other slots also point at

- Task:    B5 (menu) - the root cause F-172 named and F-176 narrowed
- Type:    FACT (census + static derivation)
- Class:   C (guest ABI/vtable slot) with an E component (what our device answers)
- Priority: P0
- Evidence: `build/w185.log` (`STREAM-OPEN` x7; all 17 frontier counters identical to
  `build/w183.log`, incl. `READWRAP 278/278` and `INFLATE-ENTER 149/149`, so the census is
  admissible); `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.14.cpp:21190`-`21250` (the store in
  `sub_821BCE68`); `ppc_recomp.17.cpp:1016`-ff (`sub_821CB488`); raw vtable words at
  `0x82012918` in `build/cache/mcla_pe.bin`; string `memory:` at `0x820127D8`

**`pgStreamer::Open`'s length store, verbatim from the listing** (`sub_821BCE68`, +0x13C..+0x170):
```
lwz  r10,-11824(r11)     // [0x8283D1F0] = a factory fnptr registered at InitClass
mtctr r11 ; bctrl        // call it with r3 = local -> creates the stream
bl 0x821cb488 (r3=local, r4=1) -> r31 = the OBJECT
stw  r31,8(r29)          // record+8  = object
lwz  r11,0(r31)          // its vtable
lwz  r10,84(r11)         // ★ slot +84
mtctr r10 ; bctrl        // obj->vt[+84](obj)
stw  r3,4(r29)           // ★ record+4 = that call's return  == the length BC140 reads
```
`sub_821BC140`'s `r30 = [record+4]` (F-172) is therefore **whatever slot +84 returns**, and
`sub_821BCB10` only searches these records by `record[0]` (F-176), so nothing else writes the field.

**Measured: `Open` runs, seven times, and the lengths are 0.** `w185`:
```
#1 r3=8EFFF770 r4=8EFFF760 r5=0000001B -> r3=00000000 lr=821E29C4
#2 .. r5=0000001B -> r3=00000001      #3 .. r5=0000001B -> r3=00000002
#4 .. r5=0000001B -> r3=00000003      #5 r3=8EFFEEB0 r4=0 r5=00000009 -> r3=00000004
#6 r3=8EFFEFD0 r4=0 r5=0000001B -> r3=00008004      #7 r3=8EFFEDC0 r4=0 r5=00001542 -> r3=0010004
```
`r3` on return is the handle id, and the executed requests carry `record[0] = 4`, `0x8004`,
`0x10004` (`REQDUMP d[0]`, F-176) - so **these three Opens are the ones the inflate loop consumes**,
and the loop then reads their `record+4` as 0.

**`r5` settles the RSC5 header argument for free.** The seven `r5` values are
`27, 27, 27, 27, 9, 27, 5442` = exactly the `+0x04` word of the seven RSC5 packages measured
offline (`legals/credits/garage/policecam/raceeditor` 27, `meshtextures.xtd` 9, `trash.xrn` 5442), and
`#5`'s `r5=9` pairs with the `READWRAP … r5=00060000` cursor that F-172 saw for meshtextures. So the
guest parses `RSC5+0x04` and hands it to `pgStreamer::Open` as a parameter - it is **not** a header
length in the "bytes of header" sense F-168 guessed; whatever it selects, the guest agrees with our
offline reading of the field, which independently validates F-171's package selection.

**Why slot +84 answers nothing.** `sub_821CB488(name, 1)` compares the first 7 characters against
`"memory:"` (string at `0x820127D8`) and on a match returns `0x827D838C` - `kMemDeviceObj`, the
device **whose vtable we install** (`kMemVtable = 0x82012918`). The raw vtable words are:
```
+0 AE50  +4 AFB8  +44 CB2A0 (Close)  +56 CABB8 (GetSize)  +80 CB400  +108 CB480  +116 CAC38
+8 249B538   +12/+28 82762480   +128 82130000
+48,+60,+64,+68,+72,+76,+84,+88,+96,+104,+112,+124  all = 0x821A5CC0   ← one shared stub
```
So slot +84 is one of **thirteen** slots pointing at the same function `0x821A5CC0` - the image's
"unimplemented virtual" thunk. If the object is the memory device, `record.length` is that stub's
return value, which is what F-172 measured as 0 and F-173/174 chased through the wrong array.

**Consequences, stated without over-reach.** (a) The UI/menu blocker is now a *missing device
capability* - answer `vt+84` on the stream object with the real size and the request gets a length,
the guest's own `InflateBegin`/XMem path gets bytes, and `swfCMD`/`XSF-INFLATE` become testable.
(b) It is NOT yet proven that the seven Opens took the `memory:` branch nor that
`0x821A5CC0` returns 0 - both are one registers-only census away: `sub_821CB488`
(`r3` = name pointer, `r4` = flag, `-> r3` = the object) and, if needed, `sub_821A5CC0` capped and
deduped by `lr` because it is a shared stub any vtable miss can reach. (c) Whatever the answer, the
fix belongs in the device vtable, not in the archive serve path - F-169/F-171 already made the
served bytes whole.

## Continuation, same session - the two devices differ at exactly this slot, and our own override is what forces the zero

Reading the two device vtables side by side from `build/cache/mcla_pe.bin` (rule 3, raw words):

| slot | packfile/archive device `0x82012BDC` | `memory:` device `0x82012918` |
|---|---|---|
| +44 | `821CD400` | `821CB2A0` (Close, the routine F-160 uses) |
| +56 | `821CD3C8` (GetSize -> `[tocEntry+4]`) | `821CABB8` |
| **+80** | **`821A5CC0` = the no-op stub** | `821CB400` (real) |
| **+84** | **`821CC498` (real)** | **`821A5CC0` = the no-op stub** |
| +88 | `821CC410` (`ld r3,16(r3); blr`) | `821A5CC0` |
| +124 | `82656BF8` | `821A5CC0` |

`sub_821CC498` decodes to `r10=[dev+0]; r11=[dev+36]; r4=r11+r4; call [r10+144](r3,r4)` - a real
sized query on the inner file object, and `pgStreamer::Open` stores **its** return into `record+4`.
The memory device answers the same slot with `sub_821A5CC0`, which is `li r3,0; blr` (4 bytes,
verified from the image). **So the archive device can supply the length and the `memory:` device
structurally cannot.**

And we make it worse: `src/gpu_device.cpp:12642`-`12646` is a **strong override of that stub** -
`PPC_FUNC(sub_821A5CC0) { ctx.r3.u32 = 0; }` with no chain to `__imp__` - installed because
`sub_8218C760` called `device+88` after GETDEV and AV'd on a null slot. It pins **all thirteen**
slots that share the stub to 0, including the archive-relevant `+84` on the `memory:` device.
Separately, our `sub_821CB488` (= `fiDevice::GetDevice`, per the Session 76j census comment at
`src/gpu_device.cpp:10990`-ff) is documented in-code as "return the memory device so the vtable+88
no-op can run" (`:10992`-`10994`) - i.e. we route some opens at the device whose +84 is a zero.

**Root cause, stated as one sentence:** `pgStreamer::Open` asks the stream's device for its size via
`vtable[+84]`; for the `memory:` device (which our own `GetDevice` override hands out, and whose
names genuinely start with `"memory:"` per the guest's own `strncmp(name, "memory:", 7)` at
`sub_821CB488+0x14`) that slot is the shared `li r3,0` stub which we additionally force to 0, so
`record.length = 0`, so the inflate loop issues a 0-byte read, so nothing ever reaches the guest's
working XMem/LZX decoder.

**Fix design (this is an implementation, not a mitigation, and is testable in one build):** give the
memory device a real `+84`. It cannot be done inside `sub_821A5CC0` (thirteen slots share it and the
address carries no information), so the options are (a) install a distinct function pointer at
`kMemVtable + 84` (`0x82012918+84`) that returns the served body's size for the handle the stream
carries - `MakeMemoryStream` already knows `{buf,size}` and `XSF-BIND` already publishes the same
number; or (b) stop handing the memory device to opens that name an archive member. (a) is the
smaller change and does not disturb F-163's re-open path. Pre-declared success criterion for F-178:
`READWRAP` with `r7=0 lr=821BC334` becomes a non-zero count, `INFLATE-ENTER`'s `st+0` stops being
`0xFFFFFFF4`, `XMEM` calls appear with per-file sizes instead of our constant 7,179,936, and only
then `swfCMD`/`XSF-INFLATE` become meaningful. Revert if `LISTLINE`/`C0000005`/`SEEK-DEAD` regress.

### F-178: F-177's last step is REFUTED by measurement - `pgStreamer::Open`'s vtable call never reaches the pinned `li r3,0` stub (its four callers are elsewhere), and this soak also proves `INFLATE-ENTER`/`READWRAP` are **timed-spin counters** that must not be used as frontier evidence

- Task:    B5 (menu) - tests F-177's inference and retires it; corrects the admissibility method used in F-173/F-177
- Type:    FACT (refutation) + FACT (measurement hazard)
- Class:   H
- Priority: P1
- Evidence: `build/w186.log` (`STUB-SLOT` 18 lines, `STREAM-OPEN` 7) vs `build/w185.log`;
  raw vtable words at `0x82012BDC`/`0x82012918` in `build/cache/mcla_pe.bin`;
  `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.14.cpp:21231`-`21241`; `src/gpu_device.cpp:12642`-ff (the stub
  override, now with the `STUB-SLOT` tally), `:11141`-ff (the `+144` hook)

**What was predicted.** F-177 argued: `Open` stores `dev->vt[+84](dev)` into `record.length`; the
`memory:` device's `+84` is the shared `li r3,0; blr` stub at `0x821A5CC0`; and we additionally pin
that stub to 0, so the length is 0 by our own hand.

**What was measured.** A per-`lr` tally inside the stub (`STUB-SLOT`, one line per new caller, cap
16, first 12 calls) shows **exactly four distinct call sites per boot**:
```
#1 lr=8217784C r3=82008F3C r4=A00011CC r5=00000040
#2 lr=8218C82C r3=827D838C r4=C81E0A80 r5=0000000A     ← the sub_8218C760 device+88 case the override was built for
#3 lr=821BE67C r3=827D838C r4=00000001 r5=0000000C     ← BE8D8/BE610 family
#4 lr=82177EF8 r3=82830B18 r4=000002D0 r5=00000001     ← hot (the remaining ~1754 calls)
```
**None of them is inside `sub_821BCE68` (0x821BCE68..~0x821BD094).** So `Open`'s `+84` call does not
land on the stub, and F-177's "the zero is our pinned no-op" conclusion is **wrong**. The inference
was reasonable and the *store site* it rests on (`stw r3,4(r29)` after `lwz r10,84(r11)`) is still
correct - only the claim about which function answers slot +84 failed.

**What the archive device's +84 actually is.** `0x82012BDC+84 = 0x821CC498` decodes to
`r10=[dev+0]; r11=[dev+36]; r4=r11+r4; call [r10+144](dev, r4)` - i.e. it forwards to **slot +144
with a name pointer built as `[dev+36] + arg`**, and slot +144 of that vtable is `0x821CBFC0` - the
packfile TOC lookup we already hook (`src/gpu_device.cpp:11141`-ff, whose `TOC76`/`TOC76-XSF` census
prints `ret=C60B7B20` = **a TOC entry pointer**). So `record+4` is fed by that lookup, and its value
in the executed records is 0 either because the name at `[dev+36]+arg` doesn't resolve on this
device, or because the field is a union that another phase overwrites. **That is the open question
now, and it is one careful read of `sub_821BCE68`+0x100..+0x180 (which value reaches the `+84` call's
`r4`) plus one `TOC76` line correlation - not another instrument.**

**The method correction, which costs nothing to keep.** `w186` vs `w185`: all 17 *structural*
counters are identical (`LISTLINE 171`, `Fatal error 0`, `FATAL-SOFT 0`, `C0000005 0`, `SEEK-DEAD 0`,
`TYPINIT 6`, `GETDEV 694`, `CP-DRAW 166`, `PRESENT 34`, `DICTLOOKUP 22`, `[error] 14`,
`STREAM-OPEN 7`, `DRAW_INDEXED 0`) - but `INFLATE-ENTER 149 → 82` and `READWRAP 278 → 138`. Those two
count the *same repeating spin* whose iteration count depends on how much wall-clock the 120 s timeout
allows, so a per-line logging footprint changes them **without changing guest progress**. Therefore:
- `INFLATE-ENTER` and `READWRAP` are **not** admissibility evidence and not progress evidence. They join
  `INFLATE`, `fatal`-substring and `nValidTag` on the run-unstable list (F-169/F-164).
- F-173's and F-177's admissibility claims were built partly on them. Those claims still hold because
  the *structural* counters also matched in both cases - but the method was wrong and is corrected here.

**Both censuses stay** (`STREAM-OPEN`, `STUB-SLOT`): each is registers-only/`lr`-keyed, bounded, and
shows zero delta on the structural frontier. `STUB-SLOT` is the only instrument that names which
vtable misses the stub is actually absorbing, which is what the eventual `+84` implementation has to
avoid breaking.

Three independent confirmations in one table: the sizes are the F-168/F-171 declared lengths

`record+4`" was aimed at a field that is not a counter.

**What that means for F-172's model.** `sub_821BC140` does
```
lwz r30,4(r28)            ; r30 = record+4 = a TOC ENTRY POINTER (non-null, per the table)
mr  r31,r21               ; candidate count = r21
cmplwi r30,32768
bge  loc_821BC2F0         ; pointer >= 32768  → KEEP r31 = r21      ← this is the taken branch
mr  r31,r30               ; (else the small value would be the count)
...
r7 = r31 → device Read(dst = r1+128, count = r7)
```
I read the comparison as a clamp of `[record+4]` and concluded the length came from that field. In
fact the comparison *dispatches on the field's type* (pointer vs count), and because the entry
pointer is always ≥ 0x10000, **the count is `r21`** - so `READWRAP … r7 = 0` means **`r21 == 0`**.
The rest of F-172 survives: the 0-byte read is measured, and the derived `st+0 = 0xFFFFFFF4` /

that field and hands it to Open as a parameter.

#2 -> id 1       rec[+4]=1,066,057  [+16]=D574B032  garage       lr=821E29C4

Every length is right and `+12` is 0 at Open time in all seven. So **F-180's conclusion is corrected**:

record is mutated by the streaming path rather than by Open.

**Direction of causality, restated from the two measurements.** `record[+4]` is a *remaining byte
count*: Open seeds it, the streamer decrements it as it reads. The inflate loop's reads are
`139/139` at `r7=0` (`lr=821BC334`) - i.e. the loop is not interleaving real reads and then a zero; it
**only ever** sees 0, and `INFLATE-ENTER`'s `consumed=32748` repeats (F-172) show it parked. Combined
with F-172's finding that all 34 `XMEM` calls are *our* replay (our `j1SrcSz=7179936`, `src` inside a
semaphore object, `ret=0`), the mechanism is:

1. `Open` seeds the record correctly (F-181).
2. The request executes; our `PPC_FUNC(sub_821D5E10)` re-point fires because the guest's
   stack-primed `st+0`/`st+4` look invalid (F-172 measured them as `-12`/`stack+12`), and points the
   inflater at a host bounce with a bogus size.
3. `XMemDecompress` returns 0 bytes, so no progress is reported; the remaining count reaches 0 (or is
   never advanced past the first window) and the loop re-enters with `r7 = 0` 139 times.
4. Nothing is ever handed to the GFx movie builder ⇒ `XSF-INFLATE 0`, `swfCMD 0`, no menu, no
   geometry.

**Therefore the experiment that has never been run** (and F-172's re-point is the thing standing in
its way): let the guest's own `InflateBegin` run against the bytes we already serve whole
(F-169/F-171), i.e. **retire the re-point** instead of routing around it. Pre-declared pass criteria,
in order: the guest's own `not in XCompress format` path becomes observable (its assert goes through
`sub_821BD618`) or `XMEM` appears with a per-file `srcSz` and `ret != 0`; then `XSF-INFLATE`/`swfCMD`
may finally move. Revert condition: any regression in `LISTLINE`/`TYPINIT`/`C0000005`/`SEEK-DEAD`/
`Fatal error`/`FATAL-SOFT` (structural counters only, per F-178).

**Censuses left in the tree** (`STREAM-OPEN` extended, `BC140-REC`, `STUB-SLOT`, `REQFILL`): each
shows a zero delta on the structural frontier, and `STREAM-OPEN`'s per-record read is now the only
instrument that shows the streamer's lengths at all.

`inPtr = stack+0x8C`, `in = 0xFFFFFFF4` - **exactly** F-172's derived `0 - 12` / `(r1+128) + 12`.
So the single attempt the guest makes is the one primed from the exhausted record (`record[+4] = 0`,
F-180), it reads a magic from the middle of the guest's own stack buffer, and it fails. Cost:

while `LISTLINE 171`, `GETDEV 694`, `CP-DRAW 166`, `PRESENT 34`, `C0000005 0`, `SEEK-DEAD 0`,
`DRAW_INDEXED 0` hold. **Reverted per the pre-declared condition** (B5 criterion 3 requires zero
`FATAL-SOFT`). Lesson, same shape as F-128's `BE710-MAGIC`: this mitigation is load-bearing, and its
removal is the only honest way to know that.

### F-186 (2026-09-24 18:35, w193) — UI containers opened but never enqueued for inflate

**Finding:** The 4 UI `.xsf` containers (raceeditor idx=0, garage idx=1, policecam idx=2,
credits idx=3) are opened through `sub_821E2940` (lr=`821E29C4`) which calls
`pgStreamer::Open` but does **not** enqueue the result for async inflate. Only the 3 non-UI
containers (meshtextures idx=4, legals idx=0x8004, trash.xrn idx=0x10004) opened through
`sub_821E5DC8` (lr=`821E5E10`) proceed to `sub_821E5E58` → `sub_821BCB10` (enqueue chooser)
→ ring buffer → `sub_821BC140` (inflate executor). Evidence: STREAM-OPEN #1-#4 lr=`821E29C4`
no ENQ; STREAM-OPEN #5-#7 lr=`821E5E10` each followed by ENQ at matching timestamp. BC140
fires exactly 3 times, all on record slot 4 with generation tags 0/1/2. W34-NOGFX fires
twice: `nGfx=0` — GFx loader never initializes because UI data stays compressed.

**Refutes F-170 truncation claim:** `xarchive_cache.rpf` is 2,130,739,200 bytes
(0x7F008000); offset 0x64CB0000 (raceeditor.xsf) has 439 MB remaining and 249/256 non-zero
bytes past the RSC5 header. All five UI packages have valid `05435352` magic and real
compressed payloads. The archive is complete; the blocker is dispatch, not data.

**Call chains decoded:**
- Non-UI: caller → `sub_821E5F48` → `sub_821E5DC8` (Open @`821E5E10`) → `sub_821E5E58`
  (enqueue @`821E5EF8`) → `sub_821BCB10` → ring buffer → `sub_821BC140`
- UI: caller → `sub_821E2940` (Open @`821E29C4`) → `sub_821BC7A0` → return (NO enqueue)

**record[+4] lifecycle resolved:** Open seeds correctly (F-181); BC140-REC shows correct
values at execution time (240,531 / 10,799); the one zero (legals rec[+4]=0 at BC140-REC #2)
is post-consumption — the inflate loop consumed it between Open and the second BC140 call.
REC4-CHANGE sampler relocated to unconditional CC6F0 entry; only one transition observed
(sentinel→0 at lr=`821BC334` = inside BC140 itself), confirming consumption not corruption.

**Next:** Either (a) make UI path also enqueue (hook `sub_821E2940` post-Open to call
`sub_821E5E58`), or (b) host-side inflate UI containers when served through this path.
Option (a) risks guest scheduling assumptions; option (b) is transparent but adds host work.

### F-187 (2026-09-24 18:50, w195) — direct UI enqueue from sub_821E2940 hook corrupts guest state

**Finding:** Calling `sub_821E5E58(structPtr, paramR5, 0, 0)` from inside the `sub_821E2940`
override after a successful open caused 3 of 4 subsequent opens to fail with handle=`FFFFFFFF`.
The first enqueue returned `0x736F7572` ("sour" in ASCII) — garbage, not a valid slot index.
Zero delta on all structural markers vs w193 baseline. Reverted to census-only hook.

**Root cause:** `sub_821E5E58` needs two descriptor objects that the UI path never constructs:
(1) inflate descriptor at r3 with context pointer at +0, handle slot at +8, secondary param at
+12; (2) data/layout descriptor at r4 with halfword counts at +0/+2 and data pointer at +4.
The UI container struct (`{+0: 0, +4: handle, +8: flags}`) is layout-incompatible with both.
Passing it as r3 produced garbage because `sub_821BC6B8` interpreted the zero at +0 as a null
context pointer.

**Safe injection point identified:** Address `0x821FE5D0` inside `sub_821FDED8`, immediately
after all 4 UI opens complete and before `sub_821C9A90`. Both branch paths converge here; no
further `sub_821E2940` calls follow. But descriptors must still be constructed first.

**Two remaining fix paths:** (A) host-side LZX decompressor (~300 lines, eliminates guest-state
dependency), or (B) construct descriptors via `sub_821E5C78` + `sub_821BC5D0` at caller level
before calling `sub_821E5E58`. Path A recommended for architectural cleanliness.

### F-189 (2026-09-24 19:39, w199) — Path A LZX is real but per-frame decode is wrong: `produced=32768` of `143069`, `rc=11` on frame 2; partial serve regresses `LISTLINE` 171→60, `TYPINIT` 6→0

**Finding:** Host libmspack LZX does expand RSC5+XCompress UI packages (Path A is not a codec gap). The first cut called `lzxd_init` per XC frame with `reset_interval=0`: only frame 0 produced output (`XSF-LZX … produced=32768 … wantOut=143069 frames=1`, `w199.log:3577`), then **rc=11** (`XC-HOST-LZX decompress FAILED rc=11 … outFilePos=0`, `:3575`). Serving that truncated body poisoned the list/type consumers — `LISTLINE 171→60`, `TYPINIT 6→0` vs `w193`. Partial output is worse than no serve.

**Fix:** Concatenate XC frame *payloads* (headers stripped) into **one** LZX stream and decode once — XCompress frames are one bitstream in 32 KiB chunks (guest keeps ctx across frames). `reset_interval=0x8000` matches the XCompress block size. **Refuse partial** (`src/gpu_device.cpp:4186-4195`): `produced + 64 < wantOut` ⇒ `XSF-LZX-FAIL`, clear `out`, fall through rather than swap a truncated body into the serve.

**Pass signal (unchanged from F-188).** `XSF-LZX >= 4` with complete `produced` and `W34-NOGFX` falling. Concat+refuse-partial is coded; not yet soak-proven (w200/w201 void — see F-190).

### F-191 (2026-09-24 19:33) — Path A is dead on arrival: an offline libmspack harness decodes `raceeditor.xsf` only to 131072 B (4×32 KiB frames) with `rc=11` under EVERY strategy and window size; supersedes F-188/F-189/F-190's Path A line and makes w202+ soaks unnecessary

- Task: T41/F-188 Path A · offline harness `tools/lzx_raceeditor_proof.c` → `build/lzx_raceeditor_proof.exe`
- Type: FACT (static proof, no soak)
- Class: D (host runtime / codec), I→resolved for Path A
- Evidence: `build/game_data/xarchive_cache.rpf +0x64CB0000` raw bytes (`05 43 53 52 … 0f f5 12 ef`, RSC5 `+0x10`=`00 02 2e dd`=143069, 37 XC frames, Σpay=142992, Σuncomp=1196032); harness stdout below; guest side `w196.log` `W27-XC-FULL` guest `0x8244FF20` reached produced=327680 (>131072)

**Harness result (raceeditor.xsf, decompressed with libmspack `lzxd.c` compiled exactly as `CMakeLists.txt:354`):**

| strategy | window_bits | reset_interval | produced | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| per-frame fresh | 17 | 0 | 32768 | frame 1 `rc=11` |
| concat one-stream | 17 | 0 | 131072 | `rc=11` at inPos=32768 |
| concat one-stream | 17 | 1 | 131072 | `rc=11` |
| concat one-stream (F-189's coded fix) | 17 | **0x8000** | **131072** | `rc=11` — same wall |
| shared-state one-lzxd | 17 | 0 | 131072 | stops after frame 3 |
| concat, window sweep | 15/16 | 0 | 131072 | head invalid |
| concat, window sweep | **17** | 0 | 131072 | **head `44 49 55 00` = "DIU" (valid)** |
| concat, window sweep | 18..21 | 0 | 0 | fails immediately |

**Why this settles it.** `window_bits=17` is the only window that yields a valid `DIU` header, confirming the format read is correct — yet every strategy caps at **131072 B = the 128 KiB window boundary**, then `MSPACK_ERR_DECRUNCH (11)`. libmspack implements **CAB** LZX; the Xbox-360 **XMem** LZX re-encodes its main Huffman tree at each aligned refresh in a way CAB decoders do not, so it diverges the instant it crosses the window boundary. No reset-interval or frame-framing choice fixes a bitstream that is structurally not CAB-LZX. The truncated 131072 the harness yields is *less* than the guest's own `0x8244FF20` achieved (327680, `w196.log`), i.e. even the partial serve is worse than what a guest-driven decode gives.

**Consequences.**
1. The F-189 in-flight fix (concat + `reset_interval=0x8000` + refuse-partial, `src/gpu_device.cpp:4186-4195`) will emit `XSF-LZX-FAIL` on all four UI containers in a valid soak (produced 131072 < wantOut 143069 − 64 ⇒ refuse), falling through to DEFLATE. It cannot pass — **w202+ soaks are not needed to learn this**; if a peer boots one and it stalls at `RD-SUBMIT<24` (F-190) it is moot regardless.
2. **Path A is closed.** The only fully-working 360 LZX decoder in the tree is the guest's `XMemDecompress` (`sub_8244FF20` / `0x82461530`), already captured via `s_xmemCtx`/`s_guestInflaterR3` (`gpu_device.cpp:3964-3965`). Any host decompression of UI must go **through the guest decoder**, not libmspack.
3. The remaining fix is **Path B** (F-187's descriptors), or a Path-B-variant: drive the *guest* inflate executor on the UI package the same way baseline drives it on meshtextures. The meshtexture inflate (`w195.log` INFLATE `#1..#5`, `lr=821BC380`, `pkg=00060000`) proves the guest pipeline works when fed; UI (pkg `0x0A0000`) simply never enters it.

**Path B — concrete implementation plan (citations current to `gpu_device.cpp` @ 20:56).**

The gap is that the UI caller `sub_821FDED8` opens each container via `sub_821E2940` (`UI-OPEN` hook `gpu_device.cpp:10200`, sets `struct{+4}=handle`) but never issues a load *request*, so the streaming executor never inflates pkg `0x0A0000`. The working non-UI request entry is `sub_821E5F48` (census hook `:10182`, comment `:10175` "called by 31 subsystems"; chain `E5F48 → E5DC8 (open) → E5E58 (enqueue) → BCB10 (chooser)` per `:10194`). F-187 failed because it called the *inner* `E5E58` with hand-built descriptors; the correct move is the *outer* `E5F48`, which builds its own descriptors.

**Enqueue ABI — decoded directly from the recompiled guest code (no IDA needed; `generated/` is read-only but readable), `generated/ppc/ppc_recomp.21.cpp`:**

`sub_821E5F48(r3,r4,r5,r6,r7)` @ `:5536` = `sub_821E5DC8(r3,r4,r5)` [open; returns `(r3&0xFF)`, 0⇒fail] then, on success, `sub_821E5E58(r3=orig_r6, r4=orig_r7, r5=0, r6=0)`. So **`E5F48` forwards its own `r6`→inflate-desc and `r7`→data-desc to `E5E58`** — the caller must build both. F-187 passed the 12-byte UI-open struct as `r3` and `0` as `r4`; wrong on both counts.

`sub_821E5E58(r3=I, r4=D, r5=0, r6=0)` @ `:5383`, exact field map:
- **`I` inflate descriptor**: `I+0` = inflater **context pointer** (`lwz r3,0(r31)` → `sub_821BC6B8`, `:5444-5450`; MUST be non-null — F-187's null here is the garbage cause). `I+4` = **out** slot index from the enqueue. `I+8` = **out** handle (alloc'd via `sub_821C9060` at `:5425-5431` when `r5==0`; freed via `sub_821C9158` at `:5505-5513` on failure). `I+12` = secondary param (`lwz r25,12(r31)` → `sub_821E58F0` r5, `:5440/5453`).
- **`D` data descriptor**: `D+0` = **u16** countA (`lhz`, `:5438`), `D+2` = **u16** countB (`lhz`, `:5464`), `D+4` = entry array base (`addi r4,r30,4`, `:5482`), **stride 12 bytes** (the `li r6,12` enqueue arg `:5478-5486`), `D+8` = result word returned on success (`lwz r3,8(r30)`, `:5524`).
- **Enqueue**: `sub_821BCB10(I+0, D+4, countA+countB, 12, r7=0, r8=handle)` (`:5472-5486`) → returns ring-buffer slot written to `I+4`. `sub_821BCB10` is the ring-B producer already instrumented at `gpu_device.cpp:8760`.

So a synthetic UI request needs only: a non-null inflater ctx in `I+0` (reuse `s_xmemCtx`/`s_guestInflaterR3` word-0 — the same context the guest's own inflate uses on meshtextures, `w195` INFLATE `lr=821BC380`), `I+12` = the container's dest/vbase, and `D` = `{countA=1, countB=0, entry[0..11] = the 12-byte BC6B8/BCB10 request record, +8=0}`.

### F-280 (2026-09-25, authoritative reconstruction of the executor window-loop `sub_821BC140` from `ppc_recomp.14.cpp`, raw-byte check of `sub_82130000`, no build) — the precise, correct F-187 root cause and fix site: the loop is gated on the pgStreamer per-window progressive-read counter, which only ever holds window 1's bytes.

- Task:        #15; `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.14.cpp` `sub_821BC140`/`sub_821D5E10` + `mcla_pe.bin:0x130000`
- Type:        FACT (mechanism) — pins the exact continue condition (supersedes the "re-serve" guess in F-278)
- Class:       C/E (guest streamer read + XMem framing)
- Priority:    P0 (objective's named deliverable)
- Evidence (`sub_821BC140` disassembly):
  - Loop-back `loc_821BC2D4`: `lwz r11,96(r1); cmplwi r11,0; bne loc_821BC374` → iterate `InflateBegin` while **dest-room `[r1+96] != 0`**; and continue-flag `[r1+112] = [r25+4]` (`loc_821BC2BC`), exit to `loc_821BC398` FLUSH when it is 0.
  - `loc_821BC2F0`: `lwz r11,29920(r22); cmpwi r11,0; bgt loc_821BC310`, else `bl sub_821C91B8` (streamer read/wait) then re-check **`[r22+0x74C0]` (streamer bytes-available)**. → the loop advances a window only while the **async pgStreamer read** has supplied the next compressed chunk.
  - `sub_82130000` (called each iteration) is a **genuine empty `blr`** (raw `mcla_pe.bin:0x130000` = `4E800020`) — a vtable no-op, NOT the culprit and NOT a recompiler bug (rule-3 verified).
  - `PATHB-UIFULL` populates the INFLATE source (`st+0/st+4`), but the STREAMER counter `[r22+0x74C0]` only ever contains window 1's bytes → after one decompress the read-gate is empty → premature FLUSH (F-279's observation, now explained).
- **Exact fix site (in-scope, `src/gpu_device.cpp`):** make the UI container's async pgStreamer read feed `[r22+0x74C0]` (bytes-available) progressively for successive `0x8000` compressed windows (from `g_destPkgWalk` over the `64CB0000`/… package) until the record's remaining `+4` reaches 0, instead of loading only window 1 — i.e., drive the STREAMER read, not the corrupt-serve. Requires modelling the `sub_821C91B8` read + the `r22` streamer-object layout (offset `0x74C0`) authoritatively (IDA-level) to avoid the recurring wrong-size model (F-253/256/262/267).

**Deliverable status:** unchanged PARTIAL, but now with a precise, verified fix target and the "why" nailed. This is the genuine F-187 enqueue gap in its original, correct form. Implementing it is a deep, high-risk change in the single most-refuted path and realistically needs IDA modeling of the `r22` streamer read + multi-cycle controlled soaks (prior route-1 authorization covers this); a blind patch is explicitly ruled out by the F-253→279 refutation history. `nGfx`=0 separate (F-277). ### F-286 (2026-09-25, cross-build isolation using the EXISTING w258 scratch test vs w262 dest-write, no build) — ROOT CAUSE pinned: the destabilizer is the **synchronous `MclaXcDecodeFullStream` CALL itself** (present in both), not the dest write. - Task:        #15; `build/w257.log`/`w258.log`/`w262.log`/`w263.log` per-dest `XMEM-SZPTR` + line counts
- Type:        FACT (root cause) — closes the "can the decompress engine be applied in-boot" question
- Class:       C/H (thread-coupling / frontier instrument)

### F-287 (2026-09-25, feasibility analysis of the remaining "non-blocking full-decompress" lever, no build) — the in-boot full decompress is blocked by a CONFLUENCE of hard constraints, not one; attempting it is a low-confidence multi-cycle redesign whose end-state payoff is unproven. This is the honest terminal analysis of the decompress-completion path.

- Task:        #15
- Type:        INFERENCE (feasibility) — completes the "is the remaining lever tractable?" audit
- Class:       A/C/D (VM reentrancy + streamer state)
- Priority:    P1
- Analysis — why the non-blocking re-architecture is not a bounded next step:
  1. **Off-thread is infeasible** — `MclaXcDecodeFullStream` calls the *guest* `sub_8244FF20` against guest ctx/stack (`gpu_device.cpp:4817-4826`); XenonRecomp guest execution is not thread-safe, so the decode cannot run on a worker thread concurrently with the guest.
  2. **Stream continuity needs persistent ctx** — LZX/XMem is one continuous bitstream with a sliding dictionary; it can't be decompressed as independent per-frame windows without holding the decoder ctx across calls (why the 64-call loop runs in one shot, F-286).
  3. **Resuming across re-entries pollutes the shared ctx** — the only way to spread the 64 calls across corrupt-serve re-entries is to persist the guest xmem ctx (shared `4000FD80`/`st=006D8F20`) between them, but the guest's OWN inflate uses that same ctx → F-286 pollution/livelock returns.
  4. **Guest double-write race** — the guest inflates window 1 into the same dest (B7B01000…) while the host would write windows 2+ → ordering/corruption risk.

### F-298 (2026-09-26 ~00:2x, existing-log content verification of `build/w271.log` + `build/w272.log` against `build/xmem_golden/*.bin`, NO build, NO new instrumentation) — the F-297 milestone claim is verified at the **guest-memory content** level, not merely the "host wrote N bytes" level: a pre-existing readback census shows each decoded dest holding the **exact golden head words** *after* the host write and after intervening guest execution. **1. What was unverified before this entry.** F-297's evidence chain was: `check_xmem_lzx` proves `host_decode_ui_xsf` byte-exact vs golden *offline*; `PATHB-HOSTDECODE* … wrote=N ok` proves the host *issued* a `WriteBytes` of N bytes that returned true. Neither proves the bytes were **still resident in guest memory** afterwards — the guest's own executor could run further windows over the same dest (the F-278/280 first-window behaviour), or the peer's `kInflateIntervene` re-point could re-serve into it. This entry closes that gap with instrumentation that already existed, so no build and no frontier-delta proof was required (cf. F-125/F-133: a *new* log line is itself a variable).

**2. The three host-decoded dests hold their golden head, after the write.** raceeditor: write at 23:45:19.577 (`:3224`), readback at 23:45:19.703 (`:3981`, and again `:3983` under the `STAR-GLOW-SEED` tag) = **+126 ms** and ~757 log lines of intervening guest execution. policecam: write 23:45:20.000 (`:14111`), readback 23:45:20.026 (`:14985`) = **+26 ms**. credits: write 23:45:20.033 (`:15204`), readback 23:45:20.041 (`:15480`) = **+8 ms**. All three match their golden's first 16 bytes exactly.

**3. The match is not a constant-pattern artifact.** `w[0]==44495500` ("DIU\0") and `w[2]==00706164` (".pad") are shared by all four containers, so alone they would prove nothing. `w[1]` and `w[3]` are **per-container distinct** — raceeditor `50036570`/`5004B2B4`, policecam `50013690`/`50015304`, credits `500140F0`/`50024884`, garage `5004E230`/`500B1B14` — and each pair equals that container's golden and no other's. Four distinct 8-byte values landing correctly is the discriminating part of the evidence.

**4. NEW, and it narrows T41.11: garage's dest is byte-correct at the head even though the host SKIPPED it.** `w271:13682` reads `@B7AC1000 44495500 5004E230 00706164 500B1B14` = garage's golden head, at 23:45:19.971 — **261 ms after** `PATHB-HOSTDECODE-TOP-SKIP #86 … room=262144 → guest` (`:4296`). So the guest's own inflate produced a correct *first window* for garage (consistent with F-274/278's all-4-first-window state), and the F-297 `fits` rule declining to write was the right call: writing the full 1,066,057 would have overrun a 262,144-byte dest, and writing a truncated prefix would have replaced valid guest output with the same valid bytes for no gain. **T41.11's real gap is therefore windows 2..N of garage (bytes ~262,144→1,066,057), not the container from zero** — and the dest is a *streaming band*, not one buffer: `JOB2-PKG-SERVE #1 dest=B7AC1000 … destCap=131072` (`w272:4295`) with the re-point walking `outPtr` across `B7AF1000`→`B7801000`→`B7809000`→`B7841000`→`B7851000` (`w272:4311`-`:4596`, `INFLATE-REFORCE #1..#12`). There is no single hook instant with 1,066,057 bytes of room, so a progressive fill must map each band slice to its offset in the decoded blob — which is the VM-state work the user deferred to its own task (directive #3). It is also adjacent to the peer's load-bearing `kInflateIntervene` re-point (F-194), so do-not #9 applies: no second re-point stacked on it.

**5. Bounded caveat — what this entry does NOT prove (class I).** (a) It compares **16 bytes per container**, not the full 143,069 / 19,337 / 29,655; whole-buffer residency in guest memory is inferred from `WriteBytes` returning true plus the head surviving, not measured. A full check would need a new readback+hash probe and its own zero-frontier-delta proof. (b) `DumpBufHead` is a **host** read of guest memory taken at the host's preload-pack dispatch census (`gpu_device.cpp:9622`), so it proves the bytes are resident and inspectable at that point in the guest's task dispatch — it does **not** prove guest code dereferenced them. (c) All eight `BUF-HEAD` lines fall inside the first ~2 s of a 120 s/300 s boot (last at 23:45:21.565 vs soak end 23:55:47), so nothing here speaks to content survival at the 5-minute mark; the dests may well be recycled later, which is irrelevant to the milestone but should not be over-read.

**6. That is the expected shape: the four UI `.xsf` are consumed by UILOAD (`sub_822C0980`) / GFx, which never runs (F-207/208, F-295, F-297 §5), not by the place-pass. The host-side consumers that *do* inspect them classify all four as `rgxa=no` and skip insertion (`D2308-INS-SKIP #1/#3/#4 … not rgxa (preload pack); AFB76-FALLBACK will serve rage_im`), which is correct — a UI `.xsf` is not an rgxa effects pack. So three byte-exact UI containers sitting resident in guest memory with no consumer arming them is exactly the F-297 §5 conclusion (decompression necessary, not sufficient; gate upstream), now observed from the consumer side as well. Two further `BUF-HEAD` hits (`@B7521000`, `@B5049000`, both `44495500 50023DE0 00706164 5006C9B4`) are a different, non-UI container and are noted only so the next reader does not mistake them for a fifth UI dest.

**Net:** the milestone "UI `.xsf` decompressed in guest memory" (user directive #1, finish line (a)) is now evidenced at content level for 3/4 containers in two independent soaks, with garage's first window also confirmed correct and its remaining gap precisely characterised for T41.11. `nGfx` still 0; the GFx wall stays closed by user decision (directive #2). ### F-299 (2026-09-26 ~00:27, funded Path A — build evidence is the exe itself, `build/f298v_build.log` is 0 bytes: `build/mcla.exe` moved 57,101,312 → **57,110,528 @00:27** and both new literals were grep-confirmed *in the image* before soaking, the F-296 stale-exe lesson; 120 s soak `build/w273.log` BOOT_RC=124, 57,969 lines) — a one-shot FNV-1a **whole-buffer** readback discharges F-298 caveat 5(a): all three host-decoded UI `.xsf` are still byte-identical in guest memory **for their entire length**, not just their first 16 bytes. Chained with the build-artifact check (`ninja -C build check_xmem_lzx` → 4/4 `EXACT`, F-297 §8), the full claim is now: **the host decoder reproduces the golden bytes offline, and guest memory holds those same bytes at full length in a live boot.** No link in that chain rests on an inference any more.

## Fleet wave F1 (2026-09-26 ~00:5x–04:0x) — four read-only research subagents dispatched in parallel on non-overlapping questions (no build, no boot, no doc writes — the tree's build/soak/ledger cycle is serial, so only *reading* parallelises). ### F-300 (2026-09-26, fleet F1 + main-agent verification) — the UI `.xsf` CONSUMER drive is still keyed on one hardcoded literal dest, while the F-297 decoder was made dynamic; this is a permitted (neither rule-2 nor F-055) and already-proven-mechanism lever at the GFx gate that has never been offered to the three decoded containers.

- Task:        T41.10 / objective's "so GFx can initialize" half; user directive #5's own reasoning applied to the consumer side
- Type:        FACT + INFERENCE (the gap is a fact; that closing it moves `nGfx` is an inference and is explicitly UNVERIFIED)
- Class:       E (serve/resource graph), G (the game's own construction path)
- Priority:    P0 (highest-value unexploited lead in this ledger as of F-300)

**1. The asymmetry.** F-297 replaced the decoder's literal `switch (outPtr)` with the dynamic `g_destPkgOff` map for a reason the user stated as directive #5 ("Hardcoded addresses will break on any boot reassignment"). **The consumer side never got that treatment.** The place/construct drive is still `constexpr kUiCont = 0xB7B41000` at `:9721`, fed to the guest's own ROOT place-pass at `:9849`/`:9861`. So the host can now decode a container into *any* dest, then only ever offers *one fixed* dest to the construction path — and in `w273` that fixed dest holds garbage (`vt=003300D9`), not a container.

**2. The mechanism is not hypothetical — it demonstrably works on a sibling.** `src/gpu_device.cpp:10390-10395` documents that `sub_825EF100` run as ROOT turns a `44495500`-headed buffer into a live object with vtable `82085364`, and `w273:6460` shows exactly that having happened to `B7521000` — the non-UI `44495500` container that F-298 §6 flagged as "a different, non-UI container". So a `44495500` buffer *can* become a claimed object in this boot, today, without any closed-wall change. The three decoded UI containers are the same container type and never get the drive.

**3. Why this is inside the permitted scope, stated precisely.** It touches no `generated/**`, no `config/mcla_xenonrecomp.toml` (so not rule-2), and it does not post/force msgid `0x40003B03` or call `sub_82131008` (so not F-055). It calls the **guest's own** compiled function that the host already calls, on a **different argument**. It is not a serve/inflate/rebase short-circuit, so do-not #9 does not bind — but it IS a behaviour change and must be flag-gated with a recorded revert path like every prior attempt.

**4. What I am NOT claiming.** That this moves `nGfx`, or that it reaches UILOAD. F-302 records that `nGfx` is a weak signal that may not be able to answer; the honest read is that this is the **only untried permitted route to the resource graph** and it is cheap to test (one build, two 120 s soaks OFF/ON). F-297 §5's "gate is upstream" conclusion stands for the *decompress* lever specifically — it was derived from "three containers resident, nothing happens", which is exactly the experiment where the consumer is pointed at a fourth, garbage dest. That derivation is therefore **weaker than it was recorded as being**, and this entry states the correction rather than leaving F-297 §5's wording standing unqualified.

### F-301 (2026-09-26, fleet F1 + main-agent raw-byte verification) — `0x82100000..0x8212FFFF` is NOT unmapped code awaiting recompilation: it is a message-subscription **DATA TABLE** lying entirely below `PPC_CODE_BASE`, so rule-2 could never have been the fix, and **F-270's stated mechanism is falsified by the bytes**. Supersedes F-270 §mechanism and F-272's reuse of it.

- Task:        T41.10 / the standing characterisation of the GFx wall (tasks #12/#15)
- Type:        FACT (+ correction of two earlier FACTs)
- Class:       A (recompiler coverage assumption), H (a log string read as a memory-protection fact)
- Priority:    P1
- Evidence:    `src/ppc_config.h:12-15` `PPC_IMAGE_BASE 0x82000000ull` / `PPC_IMAGE_SIZE 0x9E0000ull` / **`PPC_CODE_BASE 0x82130000ull`** / `PPC_CODE_SIZE 0x69D054ull` (main-agent read) · raw BE words from `build/cache/mcla_pe.bin` (off = VA−0x82000000): `0x82102AC0 = 0x82131008`, `0x82102AC4 = 0x40003B03`, `0x82102AC8 = 0x821310F8`, `0x82102ACC = 0x40002A03`, `0x82102AD0 = 0x821311A0`, `0x82102AD4 = 0x40002104`, `0x82102AD8 = 0x82131228`, `0x82102ADC = 0x4000B703`; **`0x82119C00 = 0x82516608`, `0x82119C04 = 0x40017406`** (main-agent decode) · `src/ppc_context.h:124` `PPC_LOOKUP_FUNC` indexes `(y − PPC_CODE_BASE)*2` · `src/boot_host.cpp:67` `GuestMemorySize = 0x100000000`, `:292` single `VirtualAlloc(MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE)`, `:315` image copy · `src/boot_host.cpp:376` the `"(unmapped)"` string is a **function-name lookup** result · `src/gpu_device.cpp:11282,11287` name handlers reached *via* table entries `0x8210DED8`/`0x8210DA98`, both inside the "unmapped" window, and those handlers EXECUTED

**1. The region is data, and the code-base boundary says so structurally.** `PPC_CODE_BASE = 0x82130000` (`src/ppc_config.h:14`) and the window in question ends at `0x8212FFFF` — it sits *entirely below* the first address the recompiler treats as code. `PPC_LOOKUP_FUNC` (`src/ppc_context.h:124`) computes its slot as `(addr − PPC_CODE_BASE)*2`, so addresses below the code base have no dispatch slot at all; that is why `masked >= 0x82130000u` guards exist at `src/hooks/config_dispatch.cpp:221,358`. Recompiling the window would emit **zero functions** — there is nothing there to compile.

**2. Raw-byte proof it is a `{handler, msgid}` registry.** At `0x82102AC0` the words alternate guest-code pointers and msgid-shaped values: `82131008 | 40003B03 | 821310F8 | 40002A03 | 821311A0 | 40002104 | 82131228 | 4000B703`. The first pair is the very handler↔msgid the whole GFx question is about (`sub_82131008` ↔ `0x40003B03`), sitting adjacent in the table. The fleet's wider scan reports `0x40003B03` appearing 65× against 65 distinct handlers — i.e. a broadcast registry, not a jump table. It also reports **zero `blr`/`bclr` in 49,152 words** across the 192 KiB (vs 996 and 422 in two 192 KiB code-region controls) and 43% of words being guest pointers. **The pointer/mmsgid/bl counts are the fleet's measurement, which I did not independently redo — treat the `blr` histogram as UNVERIFIED-BY-MAIN; the table shape at `0x82102AC0` and `PPC_CODE_BASE` I verified personally.**

**3. F-270's mechanism is falsified.** F-270 asserted `0x82119C04` is a jump-table row gating `sub_82131008`. The raw BE word there is **`0x40017406`** — msgid-shaped, in the same alternating-table shape as `0x82102AC4`, not a branch target (`0x82119C00 = 0x82516608` is the handler it pairs with). Two entries built on that reading need re-reading: F-270 and whatever F-272 inherited from it.

**4. "Unmapped at runtime" was a string misread, not an observation.** Guest memory is one `PAGE_READWRITE` `VirtualAlloc` of 4 GiB committed at `src/boot_host.cpp:292` with the image copied in at `:315`; `boot_host.cpp:376` prints `"(unmapped)"` when a **function-name lookup** fails. The fleet found **zero** lines in the soak logs citing an `821[0-2]xxxx` address, so there is no runtime observation of a mapping fault anywhere — the phrase entered the docs from the lookup string. Corroboration that the table is live: handlers named at `src/gpu_device.cpp:11282,11287` are reached via entries `0x8210DED8` and `0x8210DA98`, both inside this "unmapped" window, and they executed.

**5. What survives of the wall, and what does not.** The remaining, still-unexplained half is **producer-side only**: `sub_8242FD00` has 0 callers (`tools/ppc_xrefs.py calls 0x8242FD00` → `0 call site(s)`) while F-271 established the ring *consumer* compiles and works. So the honest statement is "nothing in this boot calls the DPC-post helper", not "the region holding the table is unmapped". **Caveat on the tool:** `tools/ppc_xrefs.py:136-148` never tracks `ori` (op 60), so it structurally cannot see a `lis`+`ori` msgid materialisation — its `xref 0x40003B03 → 0 sites` is weak evidence and must not be cited as a negative (same class of trap as F-057(6)). The fleet's own hand scan found 5 `lis r0,0x8210` sites, all dead (r0 overwritten before use).

**6. Consequence for task #12.** #12 is titled "Unblock GFx-init by recompiling the message-dispatch table region `0x82100000..0x8212FFFF`". Per items 1-2 that task **cannot succeed as titled** — there is no code in the region to recompile. #12 is titled "Unblock GFx-init by recompiling the message-dispatch table region `0x82100000..0x8212FFFF`". Per items 1-2 that task **cannot succeed as titled** — there is no code in the region to recompile. It should be retitled to the producer question before anyone spends a session on it. Closing it is a docs action; I am not unilaterally rewriting another session's task text beyond this note.

### F-302 (2026-09-26, fleet F1 + main-agent verification) — `nGfx` is a **weak negative signal**: its scan bands exclude every live UI/resource object address seen in the soaks, and its `0x82073xxx` vtable predicate is rejected by construction *after* the loader ctor completes. Its zero cannot distinguish "no loader was ever built" from "a loader was built and the scan cannot see one". This does not overturn any `nGfx` conclusion — it says the counter is the wrong instrument for the F-300 experiment, and names the right one.

- Task:        T41.10 (instrument hygiene for the objective's success criterion)
- Type:        FACT (the predicate/bands) + INFERENCE (that a constructed loader is therefore invisible)
- Class:       H (instrument artifact)
- Priority:    P1
- Evidence:    `src/gpu_device.cpp:6215` `int nGfx = 0;`, `:6216-6217` `kScanLo[] = {0xA0000000u, 0xC5000000u, 0xC7000000u, 0xCA000000u}` / `kScanHi[] = {0xA0800000u, 0xC6000000u, 0xC8000000u, 0xCB000000u}`, `:6218-6219` stride `0x40` over those 4 bands only, `:6223-6227` predicate `(w0 & 0xFFFFF000u) != 0x82073000u` → skip, `:6244-6249` print, `W34-NOGFX` at `:6513-6515` (all main-agent read) · live object addresses observed in `build/w273.log`: `C60AC100` (`:3947` `XSF-POSTOPEN-SERVE … dev=C60AC100`), `CB248B00` (`:6460` `FB0D8-DTOR obj=CB248B00`), `D2805C80` (`:42902`) · the ctor that re-types word0: ledger **F-044 §1** (`docs/ROOT_CAUSE_VALIDATION.md:520-531`) — `sub_82482008` installs `0x8206DFAC` via `stw r9,0(r3)` at `0x82482028` · `0x8206DFAC & 0xFFFFF000 = 0x8206D000 ≠ 0x82073000` (arithmetic, main-agent) · the honest arming signal: `MOVIE-CTOR` census `src/task_dispatch_trace.cpp:1526` (`sub_82482F78`), currently **0** in `w273`

**1. The band gap is arithmetic, not judgement.** The four scanned ranges are `A0000000-A0800000`, `C5000000-C6000000`, `C7000000-C8000000`, `CA000000-CB000000`. `C60AC100` falls in the **hole** between bands 2 and 3; `CB248B00` is above band 4's end; the three decoded UI dests `B7B01000`/`B7441000`/`B74E1000` are in no band at all. A GFx object allocated anywhere in those regions is invisible to the scan by construction, independent of its vtable.

**2. The predicate excludes the *finished* product.** `nGfx` requires word0 in `0x82073xxx`. F-044 — which this ledger already accepts — established that `sub_82482008` is a vtable-installing ctor whose store of `0x8206DFAC` lands at `[obj+0]`. If a loader passes through that ctor, its word0 becomes `0x8206DFAC`, which fails `(w0 & 0xFFFFF000) == 0x82073000`. So the scan can only ever catch an object in the **window between allocation and ctor completion**. With stride `0x40` and a `nGfx < 6` early-exit, a transient is easy to miss.

**3. This partially walks back my own F-299 wording, and I am recording it as a supersession rather than an edit.** F-297 §5 and F-299 both asserted "`nGfx` still 0" as if it were an unambiguous read of the end state. It is a read of *this counter*. Note the counter-argument, which is why this is NOT a refutation: **F-044's own headline says `W34-NOGFX` is "reporting a true fact: the guest never constructs a loader in this soak"**, and `MOVIE-CTOR` = 0 is an independent, better-targeted zero pointing the same way. So the conclusion (`nGfx` is not the right gate for F-300) is supported; the strong version (that a loader *has* been built and gone uncounted) is **not** supported by current evidence.

**4. What to measure instead, for the F-300 experiment.** Do not widen these bands (that is do-not #15 territory and it would also change an already-baselined marker mid-experiment). Use the ctor census that already exists with a real printer (`src/task_dispatch_trace.cpp:1526`, `sub_82482F78` → `MOVIE-CTOR`) plus, if needed, a **new** one-shot census on `sub_824C6F08`/`sub_82482008` — `tools/addr_owners.py` reports no current host owner for those, so rule 4 is satisfied for adding one. A new counter also needs its own zero-frontier-delta proof, per F-125/F-133 and the bar F-299 §3-4 met.

### F-303 (2026-09-26, fleet F1) — a HOST-DRIVEN multi-window fill of the garage container is **not feasible without guest-VM re-entry**, and the reason is not the one T41.11 assumed: the guest's own inflate is **stuck re-decoding frame 0**, and its output slots **clobber each other**, so writing slice *k* from the host buys nothing. T41.11 as scoped should be closed as NOT-VIABLE and re-opened only against the framing defect in item 2.

- Task:        T41.11 / task #18 (garage progressive multi-window host decode)
- Type:        FACT + FIX-analysis (negative result)
- Class:       E (serve/framing), G (guest streamer behaviour)
- Priority:    P1
- Evidence:    `src/gpu_device.cpp:8070-8081` (the `srcOff` computation; main-agent read: `uint32_t srcOff = ls.pos; … if (consumed > 0 && inPtr != 0 && inPtr < 0xA0000000u) { const uint32_t afterPos = ls.pos + consumed; if (afterPos < srcSize) srcOff = afterPos; else if (consumed < srcSize) srcOff = consumed; }` then `:8082 if (srcOff >= srcSize && IsJob2UiDest(outPtr)) served = MclaForceServePkgForDest(outPtr, st, false);`) · log gate `src/gpu_device.cpp:8132` `rn <= 32 || (rn % 50) == 0` (so `INFLATE-REFORCE` is SAMPLED, not complete) · `build/w272.log:4433` and `:4490` (`XMEM-SZPTR #12`/`#13`: identical dest `B7809000`, identical `destSz(in)=229376`, both → 0), likewise `#8`/`#9` at `B7AF1000` and `#22`/`#23` at `B7869000` · `build/w272.log:4105-4148` `PSTREAM #2 s[0..4]` (52-slot readlist, `streamCnt=52` at `:4099`) · `src/gpu_device.cpp:7515-7529` `MclaDestCapFromPstream` `default: return 0x20000u`, printed `:7757` · total guest XMem inflate calls in a 300 s soak: **24** (`grep -c XMEM-SZPTR build/w272.log`)

**1. Correction to the brief I gave the fleet, and to F-298 §3's wording.** There is no measured 128 KiB "streaming band". `destCap=131072` is a **default** returned by `MclaDestCapFromPstream` (`:7515-7529`), and the `room=262144` in the SKIP line is just `outLeft` (`st+16`) at that instant. F-298 §3's "128 KiB streaming band" phrasing should be read as "the default cap", not a measured window.

**2. The decisive defect: the source cursor never leaves frame 0.** Every sampled `INFLATE-REFORCE` in `w272`/`w273` shows `pos=00000000` and `off` only ever `0` or `0x7FEC`. Working the code at `:8074-8079`: with `ls.pos=0`, `consumed=32748`, `srcSize=32768` → `afterPos=32748 < srcSize` → `srcOff=0x7FEC`, `give=20`. On the next entry `consumed == srcSize`, so `afterPos < srcSize` is false **and** `consumed < srcSize` is false, so **neither branch assigns** and `srcOff` keeps its initialiser `ls.pos = 0`. The `ls0.pos += consumed` advance at `:8015-8020` is only on the `j2BadMag` leg. The guest therefore re-serves the start of the same 32 KiB bounce (`CB040480`, `w272:4295`) forever and never reaches frame 1 of 33.

**3. The slots clobber, so a host write would not survive.** OutPtr advances monotonically *within* a readlist slot but jumps **backward** across slots (`B7B71000` at `w272:4644` → `B7881000` at `:4660`), and `B7AF1000 = B7AC1000 + 0x30000` is an *interior* address of garage's own slot. The `#12`/`#13` pair (`:4433`, `:4490`) is the direct evidence: same dest, same incoming size, both drained to zero — the later write lands on bytes an earlier write already filled.

**4. Slot selection is not host-owned.** The caller supplies dest and size (`w272:4326 FLUSH sub_821D5510 r3=B7AC1000 r4=00040000`, `w272:4307 … lr=821D5EBC`), and `:8031-8034` only overwrites `st+20` when it already equals or poisons `outPtr`. The record itself IS freely host-readable/writable without any guest call (`:7804-7810` reads all seven fields; `:7845-7847`, `:7886-7888`, `:8104-8112` write them) — so the mechanism F-297 uses for the three single-stream containers exists; it just cannot address this problem, because the target is a 52-slot readlist whose blob-offset↔slot map no marker prints, and only slice 0..65536 is verified correctly placed.

**5. Verdict and the one measurement that would reopen it.** NO for a host-only multi-window fill. Reopening requires: a `BUF-HEAD`/`XMEM-UIHEAD` readback of each of the 52 pbase slots compared against the golden's 33-frame table, to establish whether the pack is laid out in contiguous vbase→blob order. Until that line exists the layout is UNVERIFIED. **The productive reframing is item 2**: garage's blocker is a *serve-framing* defect (cursor reset at `:8074-8079`) that also applies to any container whose final frame is partially consumed — that is a candidate for its own task, and it sits adjacent to the peer's load-bearing `kInflateIntervene` re-point, so do-not #9 governs any change there.

**Net for fleet wave F1:** the decompress deliverable is unchanged and remains banked (F-297/F-299, 3/4 at full-buffer level). What changed is the map of what is actually left: **T41.11 as scoped is not viable (F-303) and should be closed**, **task #12 as titled cannot succeed (F-301) and should be retitled to the producer question**, **`nGfx` is the wrong gate for the next experiment (F-302) — use `MOVIE-CTOR` (F-302 §4)**, and there is one **untested permitted lever at the GFx gate (F-300): the consumer drive is still pinned to the literal `0xB7B41000` while the decoder went dynamic.** Nothing in wave F1 required a build or a boot; all four agents were read-only, which is the only shape this tree parallelises in. Ledger authoritative through **F-303**; next ID **F-304**.

### F-304 (2026-09-26 ~04:1x, main-agent re-read of `src/task_dispatch_trace.cpp:1136-1196` + `build/w273.log`) — **SUPERSEDES F-300 §2 and corrects task #19's brief.** The "sibling container was consumed" evidence I cited in F-300 is a **destructor**, not a construction: `w273:6460` `FB0D8-DTOR … child=B7521000 childVt=82085364 … POISON-SKIP` is `sub_825FB0D8` = "the swf-container family destructor" (`src/task_dispatch_trace.cpp:1138`), and all 20 of its hits in `w273` are POISON-SKIP with `+4=CDCDCDCD +12=00000000`. Runs BEFORE job #2 fills B7B41000 (still CDCD)"**) · `build/w273.log` `FDBF8-BUILD #001 obj=B7521000 vt=CDCDCDCD … cnt=52685 POISON-SKIP`, `#002 obj=B7B41000 vt=003300D9 +4=004100B6 +8=0008005B arr=003100CB [arr]=00000000 cnt=61`, `#003 obj=B7B41000 vt=82085364 +4=00000000 +8=0008005B arr=003100CB [arr]=00000000 cnt=61` · `RSC-REBASE-PREPLACE-DONE obj=B7B41000 nmap=7 headRewritten=0 childRebased=0 childGate=0 nestPass=1/2/3` (`w273:~42500`, 3 lines) · marker counts in `w273`: `FDBF8-ARR-RESTORE` **0**, `PLACE-ARR-RERUN-DONE` **0**, `PLACE-ARR` **0**, `825FDA90` **0**, `FB0D8-DTOR` 20 (all POISON-SKIP) · gate that skips the restore: `src/gpu_device.cpp:9851` `const bool realVt = (vt & 0xFFFF0000u) == 0x82080000u;`

**1. What F-300 got wrong, stated plainly.** I recorded `w273:6460` as "proof a SIBLING container did get consumed". It proves the opposite: the object at `B7521000` reached the **destructor** with a stamped vtable and an **uninitialised body**, and the host guard deliberately returned early rather than free it. A vtable of `82085364` + `+4=CDCDCDCD` is precisely the case the w1a comment describes — "a place-pass can write vt=82085364 onto an otherwise-CDCD buffer" (`src/task_dispatch_trace.cpp:1156-1159`). **The lever F-300 proposes is therefore not "already proven on a sibling"; its mechanism is unproven and its failure mode is already known** (virtual dispatch through such a vtable AVs at `825FB14C`). The `grep` I ran confirmed the line exists; it did not confirm what the line *means*. My error, not the agent's — I read a marker's text without reading its printer.

**2. The correct Path B statement, which is now much sharper than F-300's.** `sub_825EF100` (place-pass) does four things: calls FDBF8 to build, stamps `vt=82085364`, rebases `[obj+24]`, and **walks entries via `sub_825FDA90`**. For the walk to yield anything, the object's body must be a real descriptor array. What `FDBF8-BUILD #002/#003` show at `B7B41000` is the body holding **raw inflated RSC bytes where a struct is expected**: `vt=003300D9`, `+4=004100B6`, `+8=0008005B`, `arr=003100CB`, and `arr` dereferenced is `00000000`. Every one of those is little-endian-looking payload data, not a guest pointer. So Path B = **construct the container-object descriptor block** — a valid vtable, a valid `+4` child, a valid `arr` at `+12`, `cnt` at `+16`, and `[obj+24]` rebased — **whose entries point into the decoded UI payload that Path A already put in guest memory byte-exactly.** That is the literal objective wording ("guest descriptor construction"), and it is now correctly scoped.

**3. The host already tries this and provably does nothing — three independent zeros.** `FDBF8-ARR-RESTORE` (`src/gpu_device.cpp:9800-9833`, the `kArrCand[]` guess list) fires **0** times, because it sits inside `if (realVt)` at `:9851` and `B7B41000`'s `vt=003300D9` fails that test — the exact garbage F-300 §1 noted, now with the causal chain. `PLACE-ARR-RERUN-DONE` (`:10382`) fires **0** times. And `RSC-REBASE-PREPLACE-DONE` fires 3× with `nmap=7` but **`headRewritten=0 childRebased=0 childGate=0`** — it built a 7-entry vbase→pbase map and replaced **nothing**. So "point the existing machinery at the decoded dests" (my original #19 brief) would inherit a code path that is already running and already yielding zero. **#19 as written would have produced a null result and I would have mis-attributed it.**

**2. CORRECTED — `[obj+12]` is an advancing CURSOR, not a relative offset, and my first reading of it was wrong.** The draft of this item claimed the guest rebases `+12` by adding a *base*, which would have made `FDBF8-BUILD`'s `[arr]=00000000` an ABI artifact and revived a "the payload IS the header" theory. The full disassembly of `sub_8217D890` refutes that: its return value is `8217D8C8 lwz r10,8(r11)` / `8217D8CC lwz r9,4(r11)` / **`8217D8D0 subf r3,r9,r10` → `table[idx].+8 − table[idx].+4`, a LENGTH** (`8217D8B0 cmpi cr6,r3,-1` makes −1 "not found"). So `825FDC34 add r10,r3,r11` is **`[obj+12] += length`** — consume a block, advance the cursor. A cursor must start as a real pointer, and `0x003100CB` is not one (below every guest heap address). **Consequence: F-304 §2's diagnosis STANDS — the body at `B7B41000` is raw inflated payload where a struct belongs, the descriptor is genuinely unfilled, and Path B does have to construct one.** Two claims from my draft are withdrawn: (i) "`[arr]=00000000` is an instrument artifact" — it is a correct read of a garbage cursor; (ii) "writing an absolute candidate is ABI-wrong" — **absolute is exactly what the cursor wants**, so `src/gpu_device.cpp:9826` is right in kind and fails only because it never runs. **2b. Cursor semantics also name the exact gap.** FDBF8 **skips the consume entirely when `[obj+12] == 0`** (`825FDC20 cmpli cr6,r4,0000` → branch to `825FDC3C`), so a null cursor is the guest's own "nothing to build" signal. That is precisely what the project's own comment describes — "the container whose [+12] entry array stays CDCD when **the preload task never fills it**" (`src/task_dispatch_trace.cpp:1071-1073`). In other words the objective's F-186/F-187 **enqueue gap restated in ABI terms**: the descriptor's cursor is *produced by the preload task*, and for these containers it never arrives.

**3. `FDBF8-BUILD #002/#003` re-read under the cursor semantics — original diagnosis survives.** `w273`: `obj=B7B41000 vt=003300D9 +4=004100B6 +8=0008005B arr=003100CB [arr]=00000000 cnt=61`. I briefly thought `arr=0x003100CB`/`cnt=61` might be a genuine header misread as garbage; item 2 kills that, because a `+= length` cursor has to start as a real pointer and `0x003100CB` is not one. `cnt=61` from a `lhz` and a byte-swapped payload fragment are indistinguishable without the pointer test, so nothing here rescues the buffer. **Verdict unchanged from F-304: the descriptor is unfilled and must be constructed.** Worth keeping from the attempt: `+0`, `+4`, `+8`, `+12` are ALL sub-`0x80000000` values, i.e. no field of the "object" is a pointer, which is the cleanest single-line proof that place-pass stamped a vtable onto a buffer that was never a struct.

**4. The entry-record format, partially decoded — enough to bound the work.** `sub_825FDA90` is a 9-way switch on a **u8 type tag at `[rec+8]`** (`lbz r4,8(r3)`; `addi r10,r4,-1`; `cmpli …,0008`), so tags **1..8 are valid** and anything else branches to the error object `0x82087180` via `sub_821BD618` (`825FDB24-825FDB2C`). Table read back from the image: tag1→`82609350`, **tag2→`825FDBF8` (recurses into the build pass — nested containers)**, tag3→`826078C8`, tag4→`82607098`, tag5→`826059B0`, tag6→`82604FF0`, tag7→`82605058`, tag8→`82606FB0`. Note the tag is read at `+8` while FDBF8's loop uses stride 8 — so a record's type byte is the first byte of the *following* 8-byte slot, i.e. the records FDBF8 strides over are not the same units `FDA90` switches on. **UNVERIFIED:** the exact record unit each consumes. Getting this wrong is precisely how "walk garbage" produced the historical Resource fatal, so it must be settled before any descriptor is written.

**1. The rule that made it work is F-320's, applied as a write instead of a read.** Consecutive readlist slots tile one contiguous virtual range, so a container larger than any single slot must be laid out across them at `slot.vbase − anchor.vbase`. `w293` confirms the guest agrees: the fill's four slots are `vbase 50000000/50040000/50080000/500C0000` with sizes `0x40000/0x40000/0x40000/0x8000`, and the run stops at 819,200 because **the job's slot run ends there**, not because of any cap in the fill.

**2. `vbase` is per-job — discovered by the protection that saved us.** Two `-SKIP` lines fired for the garage, naming `B7B01000` and `B7B61000`: those are **raceeditor's** slots, which the span test matched because raceeditor's job also starts at `vbase 0x50000000`. Without the "only overwrite poison/zero" rule this change would have silently corrupted a container already measured at 100 %. **Rule kept for anyone extending this: a `vbase` is meaningful only inside its own job — never use it as a global address space.** (F-297's directive-#5 lesson, one level up: not just dests but *virtual bases* are re-used per job.)

**3. Two of my own instrument readings were wrong and the fixes are now in the code.** (a) `w291`/`w292` reported `goldoff=00000000 mismatch=0` for all four filled slots even though they hold different golden ranges, and `bytes_exactly_covered=819200`. Widening the needle from 16 to 64 bytes did not fix the offset ambiguity, so `gold_span` from the fill is the field to cite, not the hunt's `goldoff`. Explanation: the LZX decode is **one continuous bit stream across frames** — the driver's frame offset and saved cursor are not stale junk to be cleared, they are the stream position, and clearing them while *also* moving `src` to a different buffer puts the bit cursor at a place that is not where the bytes are. The latched no-op of F-332 was a *symptom*; both halves (src and resume state) have to agree, and only the guest knows the pair. **That closes the whole "re-point `st+4`" family, which is what our serve has done since F-318 — including the variants that "advanced `consumed`" (F-320, F-329) and the ones that didn't (F-327, F-333).**

Both new flags are `false`; the instruments from F-331/F-332 stay in (they measured +0 against every control).

**5. What Path B must do instead** (now the only remaining shape that respects the contract): **do not move `src`.** Fill the container's continuation bytes *into the buffer the guest is already pointing at*, at `st+4 + st+0`, and raise `st+0` by what was written, so the driver's own `[S+12276]`/`[S+12280]` pair stays internally consistent. The prerequisite, and the only genuinely new work in it, is deriving the package offset that corresponds to the guest's current buffer position — obtainable without guessing by locating the tail of the guest buffer's existing content inside the package bytes we already hold host-side. Nothing in the tree does this today; `MclaUiXsfChunkOpen`'s refill is the place it belongs.
