### F-397 (2026-09-26 22:2x, **2 builds, soaks `w414`/`w415`; two log-only probes in the tree**) — **CLAUSE (b) IS FULLY ROOT-CAUSED. The boot worker's "hang" is the title's own free-list initialiser `sub_82397060` entered with a count of 0: its only guard is `count-1 == 0`, so `r11` starts at `-1` and the link loop at `loc_82397184` cannot terminate until 4 294 967 295 iterations — and the stores it performs match the observed garbage at our heap header word for word (`[p+12] = p+16`, so `guest=0x20000 val=0x20004`, `guest=0x20010 val=0x20014`, …). F-370's "deterministic garbage", F-384's "the writer follows the arena base" and F-394/5's "never returns" are this one loop.**

- Task:        T41.73/T41.74 (objective clause (b)); supersedes F-396 §3's "the sweep length is unknown" and closes tasks #41/#43 (the hand-off) as a *consequence*, not a cause.
- Type:        FACT (+ two log-only probes).
- Class:       G (the game's own coded behaviour) — reached through C/D facts.
- Priority:    P0
- Evidence:    `build/w415.log` — `WATCH: range armed [828CD064,828CD074)` @22:22:00.690 → `F395-GROW-ENTER #1 obj=828CD064 want=0 lr=823973C0` @22:22:14.517 → `F397-OBJ #1 obj=828CD064 [+0)=00000000 [+8)=00000000 [+16)=00000000` → `PAGEWATCH W #05 @ 828CD064 = 00000001 lr=82397068` → `PAGEWATCH W #06 @ 828CD06C = D3CDF800 lr=823970F4` → 8.24 s later `F374-HEAPSTORE #1..#16 guest=00020000,00020010,… val=0x20004,0x20014,… caller_rva=0x141bb85 tid=19432` · `python tools/host_rva_resolve.py build/mcla.map 0x141bb85` → `__imp__sub_82397060 + 0x345` · code: `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.61.cpp:17888-17923` (the loop), `:18240-18250` (the only call site, in `sub_823971D0`) · probes: `src/gpu_device.cpp:17208-17236` (F397-OBJ + widened F396 cap), `src/boot_host.cpp:1706-1717` (the `0x828CD064` watch).

**1. The loop, verbatim (`ppc_recomp.61.cpp:17888-17923`).** `r30` is the second argument:

    loc_82397164:  r11 = r30 - 1;  [r31+12] = r10; [r31+4] = r8; [r31+16] = r10;
                   if (r11 == 0) goto loc_823971A0;          // <-- the ONLY guard: count == 1
                   r10 = r8;  r7 = r11;
    loc_82397184:  r9  = [r31+16];  r11 = r11 - 1;  r9 = r9 + r10;
                   r10 = r10 + 16;  r6 = r9 + 16;  [r9+12] = r6;
                   if (r11 != 0) goto loc_82397184;          // bne on CR0.EQ of r11-1

With `r30 = 0`, `r11` starts at `0xFFFFFFFF`; the branch is on equality with zero, so the loop runs
**4 294 967 295 times** and each iteration writes a link `[X+12] = X+16` while `X` advances by 16 from
the freshly-allocated block. The measured F374 rows are exactly that shape: store at `0x20000` with
value `0x20004` ⇒ `X = 0x1FFF4`, `X+12 = 0x20000`, `X+16 = 0x20004`; store at `0x20010` value
`0x20014` ⇒ `X` advanced by 16. **Two claims I am NOT making:** the sweep's *step* is not constant
(`r9` is `[r31+16] + r10`, and `[r31+16]` is rewritten inside the loop, so the address sequence is not
a plain 16-byte march and I have not worked out its closed form), and the iteration count is an
arithmetic consequence of the guard, not a measurement.

**2. Where the zero comes from.** The only call site in the whole image is
`ppc_recomp.61.cpp:18240-18250`, inside `sub_823971D0`:

    lis  r11, -32115 ; addi r31, r11, -12188   -> r31 = 0x828CD064   (the static container)
    lhz  r4, 4(r28)                            -> the count, a 16-bit field of *r28*
    mr   r3, r31 ; bl 0x82397060
    lhz  r11, 4(r28) ; cmplwi r11, 0            <-- the caller checks for ZERO only AFTER the call

So `sub_823971D0` legitimately expects `[r28+4]` to be able to read 0 — and the callee's guard makes a
0 fatal-but-silent. Measured: it is 0 in this boot (`want=0`), and the container was empty at entry
(`[+0]/[+8]/[+16]` all 0), so nothing about this container was ever populated.

**3. What this retroactively explains.** (a) F-370's "deterministic garbage at the o1heap header" —
it is a link list being built through it. (b) F-384's "move the arena and the writer follows it" — the
sweep passes through whatever base we chose, so the follower was never a hand-off; **tasks #41/#43 were
asking the wrong question and are closed by this.** (c) F-394/F-395's one-enter/never-exit and the
`PARAM-STORE` cycle at `0xA0106000..0xA01067F0` (same `[p]=p+4` shape, under the frozen
`lr=82397124`). (d) Why a 300 s soak changes nothing (F-394 §4): 4.3e9 iterations at any plausible
recomp speed is minutes-to-hours.

**4. Consequence for the objective — and it is good news for clause (a).** Clause (b) is *not* gated on
GFx, not on the UILOAD registration, not on the shared inflate record: it is gated on
**`[r28+4] != 0`**. Everything the F-186/F-187 line has been chasing (enqueue, descriptors, records) sits
behind a thread that is busy for the rest of the process. T41.75: identify the object `r28` is (read
upward in `sub_823971D0` from line 17957, where the function starts, to 18242 for its assignment) and
then determine who is supposed to fill its `+4` halfword — that name, not another inflate instrument, is
the next thing to write down. If it is one of the UI .xsf consumers, clause (a) and clause (b) finally
become the same task. Next ID **F-398**.

### F-432 (2026-09-27 00:2x, **0 builds — static reads of `generated/` + the raw image, plus a re-read of `w430`**) — **THE BOOT-WORKER LivelOCK AND THE HEAP-HEADER STORM ARE THE SAME BUG: `sub_82397060` is entered with `count == 0`, and its free-list link loop is guarded on `EQ` only, so it then runs 2^32-1 times storing `[r9+12] = r9+16` over the whole 32-bit guest space.**

- Task:        T41.87 (this supersedes its declared first step — the writer of `[record+1540]` turned out not to be the blocker; the count-0 storm was), and it closes the open half of #48 / the F-371/F-384 hunt.
- Type:        FACT
- Class:       G (the title's own coded behaviour) with a D consequence
- Priority:    P0
- Evidence:    `build/w430.log` `F395-GROW-ENTER #1 obj=828CD064 want=0 lr=823973C0 sp=8EFFF640` (the only ENTER row in the soak, `F395-GROW-EXIT` 0) · `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.61.cpp:17859-17923` (the two loops), `:18237-18258` (the caller) · `build/cache/mcla_pe.bin` VA 0x82051E90 = `"Vehicle"` (offset 0x51E90, bytes read directly)

**1. The caller is single and it passes a zero halfword.** `sub_82397060` has exactly one call site reached in this boot, inside `sub_823971D0` at `0x823973B4`: `lis r11,-32115` + `addi r28,r11,-12120` = **0x828CD0A8**, and the argument is `lhz r4,4(r28)`. `0x828CD0A8` is zero-fill (the eight words there read `00000000` straight out of `mcla_pe.bin`), so `want` is 0 unless something raises it first.

**2. Why 0 is catastrophic, in the routine's own words.** With `r30 = count`: the zero-fill loop (`ppc_recomp.61.cpp:17859-17886`) is entered only after `addic. r11,r30,-1` + `blt skip` — a *signed* test, so count 0 (r11 = -1) skips it. The link loop at `loc_82397184` (`:17888-17923`) is guarded by `addic. r11,r30,-1` + **`beq` skip** — equality only. Count 1 skips, count 0 falls in with r11 = -1 and `bne` keeps looping until the counter wraps: 4,294,967,294 iterations. Each stores `[r9+12] = r9+16` with `r9 = [r31+16] + r10` and `r10 += 16`, i.e. a stride walk by `(allocPtr+4)` through the *entire* guest address range, wrapping. That is the "deterministic garbage" F-371 named, and the reason F-384 observed "the writer follows the arena base" — the stride *is* the freshly allocated pointer. It also explains F-395's enter-without-exit, and why everything downstream of it in the boot was uninterpretable.

**3. Why the halfword is 0 (F-405's question, answered one level up).** The walk that raises it is `loc_82397328` in the same function: `sub_821CFF40(&[r1+144], r29, 0)` with `r29 = 0x82051E90` = the string `"Vehicle"`, and only when that lookup returns non-zero does the caller reach `mr r3,r28; li r4,16; bl sub_82396DF8` — **add 16 entries per found section** (`:18199-18206`). The lookup returns 0, so it jumps straight to the grow call with the count still 0. `tools/ppc_xrefs.py xref 82051E90` gives exactly one site (0x823972ec), so this is the only consumer of that name in the image. Neighbouring strings at 0x82051EA0 / 0x82051EC8 are `AllocateCarData - %s.lst not found` and `/vehicle/vehicle%04d`.

**4. Consistent with, and sharpening, F-400/F-401/F-405.** `F401-GROUP` at the same millisecond shows >= 16 group descriptors already linked on the head at `0x828559E4` (that walk is capped at 16 rows, so read it as "at least"), each with `[+4)=0 [+8)=0` — the groups are *registered* and never *bound*, which is exactly what a failed section lookup produces. So task #49/T41.76's "producer that must raise the count" is now named: `sub_82396DF8(0x828CD0A8, 16)`, gated on the "Vehicle" section lookup, and nothing in `src/` publishes that field.

**5. What this does NOT establish.** No evidence yet that the "Vehicle" lookup is *supposed* to succeed at this point in the boot (an ordering question), nor which archive feeds it; and no evidence that removing the storm is sufficient for GFx — F-433 measures what actually happens when it does not run.

### F-434 (2026-09-27 00:4x, **2 builds, soaks `w431`/`w432`; MITIGATION KEPT, VERIFIED**) — **BREAKING THE NON-UI INFLATE SPIN IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE ADVANCE OF THIS WAVE: the boot stops burning its last 105 s in one loop and the pipeline continues — `BC140-REC` 5 -> 7 (two new streamer records reach `sub_821BC140` for the first time), `W34-GFX-CENSUS` 3 -> 6 with the first NON-POISON GFx object ever seen here (`vt=82085364`, `nLiveDest=4`, `tagNv=2`), and the garage's coverage regression from F-433 disappears. `nGfx` is still 0.**

- Task:        T41.88 (new head; T41.87's premise is superseded by F-432)
- Type:        FIX (a named mitigation of a guest infinite loop, not a decompression fix)
- Class:       G + D
- Priority:    P0
- Evidence:    `src/gpu_device.cpp:1088-1097` (flag `kF434BreakNoProgressSpin`), gate + drain at `src/gpu_device.cpp:11007-11042` · `build/w432.log` (`F434-SPIN-BREAK` at 1 firing) vs `build/w431.log`, `tools/soak_census.py build/w432.log build/w431.log` and `.. build/w193.log`

**1. The loop had no exit because every existing exit is UI-only.** Both drains in the place pass require either `produced > 0` (`INFLATE-UNSTUCK`, `src/gpu_device.cpp:10986-10995`) or a UI/job2 dest (`INFLATE-J2-CONT`, `:11008+`). `w431`'s spinner is `PSTREAM #5 s[4]` of readlist `8284B37C` — `BC140-REC #5`, the stream whose record field `+24` is `0x000A0000` — F-318 §1 called that stream "meshtextures" and the `w418/w419` handoff block called it "legals.xsf", so **its name is unsettled in our own docs**; what is settled is that `0x000A0000` is a *length* field (655,360), not a package VA, and that F-318 identified this same `st=006D8F20` shape as the dominant one — with `produced=0`, `inLeft=20`, `outLeft=524288`, `consumed` frozen at 32,748 and `magic=3B6426F9` (neither `0x05435352` RSC5 nor an XCompress header). `sub_821BC140` cannot leave by itself: `loc_821BC2D4` tests the owed-output word at `[r1+96]` first and branches straight to the place call, so while output is owed it never issues the next read (`ppc_recomp.14.cpp:19040-19050`, `:19128-19170`) — placement needs input and the input read is the skipped step. 23,155,400 iterations of that.

**2. What the mitigation does, and the predicate that keeps it honest.** After 64 consecutive sightings of the *same* `(st, consumed)` with `0 < inLeft < 256`, `outLeft > 0`, `produced == 0`, it writes `[st+0] = 0` and `[st+16] = 0` — the caller loop's own stream-complete key, mechanically identical to what `INFLATE-UNSTUCK` already does for UI dests, in the same scope, same `mem` accessor, same guest-stack object. Requiring `consumed` to be **frozen** (not merely "produced 0") is what makes it unable to fire on a legitimately mid-frame stream, where `consumed` rises and `inLeft` cycles. It fired **once** in the whole boot.

- Task:        T41.95 (new head) — corrects F-443
- Type:        FACT

- Priority:    P0

**1. The three measured states (`w447`, all 14 rows, all `ret=0`, `hits=0`).**
- `#1-#4 name='shadinggroup' r5=1`: `mode=13 inner=82860C40 data=82861DF8 pos=46 len=485..480`, and the buffer is **real config text** — `head='Version: 103..shadinggroup {..Sh'`. So a section literally named in the buffer still ends the enumeration.

**4. ### F-457 (2026-09-27 03:5x-04:0x, **3 builds, soaks `w459` (probe at the wrong site → 0 rows) and `w460` (81 rows); probe KEPT, log-only**) — **THE TUNE STREAM'S STARVED INFLATE IS NOW PINNED TO THE F-186 PLACE PASS, AND THE `memory:$` BLOCK DUMP CLOSES Path A FOR THE CONFIG TEXT: no block the guest wraps is an XMem/RSC container (0 of 81 start `52534305`/`EF12F50F`), the only plaintext block is a mid-token tail of a SHADERS list, and not one block carries a tune path. **1. ### F-459 (2026-09-27 04:1x, **0 builds — windowed read of `w460` between the two nested-archive opens and the tune `.lst` NULL**) — **THE NESTED MOUNT NEVER ADVANCES: in the 906-line window from `BDF20 #590 (preload/xarchive_cameratune.rpf)` to `BDF20 #600 (tune/vehicle/vehicle0008.lst, ret=0)`, our VFS prints `opened REAL packfile 'xarchive_cache.rpf'` 101 times, the nested archive is never opened as a packfile at all, and all 141 buffered reads in the window are `cnt=32768` with `reqPos=00000000_0000` — the same position 0, alternating between two 32 KiB buffers, forever.**

- Task:        T42.5 — answered without a build (the existing markers covered the mount window)
- Type:        FACT + host-side defect candidate (re-open storm / position never advances)
- Class:       E (filesystem/device), with an H component (our VFS's own log is the evidence)
- Priority:    P0 — this is where clause (b)'s chain actually breaks, one layer above F-458

**1. What the window shows.** The guest asks for a `0x35A000`-byte read through wrapper `C64B7600` and gets `ret=00000000` (zero bytes) with `r1in == r1out == 006D8EC0` — the read position does not move — and this identical request repeats ~198 times across 0.16 s. So the mount of the nested archive is not merely failing at content (F-458 §2): the code path that would mount it is re-entered on the outer archive instead, with a zero-length read at position 0.

**2. Why this is a defect candidate and not just a guest behavior.** `r4=C64B7600` and `r5=0035A000` are constant across all 198 rows and `ret=0` every time; a guest stuck in its own retry loop would still normally move `r1in`. `r1in == r1out` plus `ret=0` is the signature of a read handler that reports success without consuming anything, which is the same failure shape as F-331/F-383's "the routine returns S_OK and produced nothing". Our own serve layer is the thing answering reads on `C64AC100`, so the first place to look is the read path keyed by that wrapper (`lr=821CCDBC`, inside `sub_821CC6F0`), not the guest.

**3. Consequence for the objective's two clauses.** Clause (a) stands as measured (3/4 UI `.xsf` byte-exact, garage 94-100 % durable). Clause (b) does not need an inflate, a record, a gate bit or a decoder at this point (F-446/F-450/F-454/F-456/F-457/F-458 each closed one of those): **it needs the nested archive's read to return bytes and advance**. The next concrete step is therefore narrow and cheap: one build, log-only, at `sub_821CC6F0`'s read handler — print, for requests on wrapper `C64B7600` (and for any read whose `r5` exceeds the served window), the branch that produced `ret=0` and `r1out`, so the zero is attributed to a named site in `src/` rather than inferred. Acceptance: the site is named, and then a single-variable fix attempt can be judged by whether `reqPos` advances and whether `BDF20` for the tune `.lst` stops returning NULL (F-458 §1 is the yardstick: `ret=0x82860C40` instead of `0`).

**4. Also recorded because it will be mistaken for progress:** `INFLATE-ENTER` and `INFLATE-J2-LAST-JUNK` each print 99 times inside this window — that is the place pass spinning on the same stale record (F-434's shape) and it is *not* decompression progress; `produced` stays 0 there (F-457). ### F-461 (2026-09-27 04:1x-04:2x, **2 builds - one attempted fix, measured and reverted; tree restored and verified**) — **THE `sub_821CC6F0` SERVED-BODY BRANCH IS STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE, AND THE BLOCKER IS TWO LAYERED: (a) the call site at `src/gpu_device.cpp:14753-14755` passes `handle=0xFFFFFFFF` and `tocEntry=0`, while since F-091/F-126 those are the only indexes that can still return true - every other index just logs `T413O-SKIP ... would-serve` and the function ends in `return false` (:1780); and (b) even when a body IS resolved, these requests arrive with `r7=0` from `lr=0x821BC334`, which takes the deliberate w21/w22 `READWRAP-R7Z` lever that returns 0 on purpose so the guest proceeds into `InflateStep`.**

So restoring the key alone would deliver no bodies on the inflate refill path either; the two layers have to be reasoned about together, and any future attempt must key on the request rather than on the device.

### F-462 (2026-09-27 04:2x, **0 builds — the guest's own recompiled routine read, plus a census of all 14,363 `READWRAP` rows in `w460`**) — **WHAT `sub_821CC6F0` ACTUALLY IS, AND IT CORRECTS F-459'S FRAMING: it is not a per-file read. Per `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.17.cpp:3931-3996` it takes `(obj, r4, offset, dst, count)`, resolves an inner stream at `[obj+32]`, calls inner vtable+132, then calls inner vtable+28 with `r5' = [obj+24] + offset`. Measured across the whole boot: `r3` is ALWAYS `C64AC100`, `inner=[r3+32]` is ALWAYS `C6537780`, `r4` is ALWAYS the request block `C64B7600[98B0D2B1 F77F0000 0 0]` — the only thing that varies is the offset, and it takes exactly five values. So this is one stream addressed by absolute archive offset; and the nested tuning archive's offsets never appear here at all.**

- Task:        T42.7 — answers the prerequisite F-461 §3 named, with no build
- Type:        FACT + CORRECTION (supersedes F-459 §1/§2's attribution of the zero reads; F-459 §2's offline arithmetic stands)
- Class:       E (archive/device layer) + H (our own attribution of these rows)
- Priority:    P1 — it retargets where the nested-archive read is even issued
- Evidence:    `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.17.cpp:3931-3996` (`mr r31,r5` → `lwz r3,32(r30)` → `lwz r11,0(r3)`/`lwz r10,132(r11)`/`bctrl` → `ld r11,24(r30)`/`add r5,r11,r31` → `lwz r9,0(r3)`/`lwz r8,28(r9)`/`bctrl`) · `build/w460.log`: 14,363 parsed `READWRAP … inner=` rows → `r3` 1 distinct, `inner` 1 distinct (`C6537780`), `r4` 1 distinct, and 5 distinct offsets `64CA7B89` ×10,251 · `0035A000` ×1,287 · `64CB0000` ×1,216 · `649763D7` ×1,005 · `000A0000` ×604

**1. The routine, read rather than inferred.** `sub_821CC6F0` = "seek-and-read through the inner stream": `r30=obj`, `r29=r4`, `r31=r5`, `r28=r6` (destination), `r27=r7` (count). It first calls `[ [obj+32] + 132 ]`, then computes `r5' = [obj+24] + r31` and calls `[ [obj+32] + 28 ]` with `(r4, r5', dst, count)`. Our hook already reads `[r3+32]` and prints it as `inner=` — which is what let this be settled from existing rows instead of a new probe.

**2. Why the "per-file handle" F-461 §3 asked for does not exist here.** Nothing in the registers names a file, because the file is named by the **absolute archive offset** in `r5`. All five observed offsets lie inside `xarchive_cache.rpf` (2,032 MB): `0x64CB0000` (raceeditor's package region), `0x64CA7B89`, `0x649763D7`, `0x0035A000`, `0x000A0000` (meshtextures). A safe serve at this site therefore keys on `r5` against the TOC's member ranges — data we already hold — and unlike the device scan of F-461 it cannot cross-serve, because the offset is a property of the request.

**3. The correction, against F-459's own numbers.** F-459 read the 198 identical zero-byte rows inside the tune window as "the nested mount never advancing". They are `r5=0035A000` rows — **meshtextures package refills** on the shared stream, i.e. F-457's stale-record spin, not mount traffic. The nested archives' own offsets (`0x48000` carconfigs, `0x68000` cameratune, from `TOC76-XSF #1428/#1430`) appear **zero times** as `r5` in the entire boot. So the guest never asks this stream to read the nested archive: the tune mount is attempted (or abandoned) somewhere else, and the 101 `VFS: opened REAL packfile 'xarchive_cache.rpf'` rows in that window are our own outer-archive re-mounting. F-459 §2 (single `RPF3` header, no data base landing on a header) and F-458 §1 (`BDF20`'s field is the stream object; the tune `.lst` yields NULL) are untouched and still stand.

**4. Next, named rather than guessed.** The tune open did produce a stream object (`0x82860C40`), so whatever would read the nested archive is that object's own path — and F-449/F-456 already show its `[+24]/[+28]` walking a stale buffer while the fetch branch (`sub_821BDD28`) prints 0 rows. So **T42.8** is one log-only probe on `obj=0x82860C40` inside `sub_821BE250`/`sub_821BE4F0`: print the target offset it resolves, whether inner vtable `+132`/`+28` were entered for it, and what the device answered — which is the first time the nested mount itself is observed instead of inferred.

**5. Addendum, checked the same pass because it bounds any "just decrypt it" plan.** The local upstream checkout offers no key and no reference implementation for this container type: `.research/xenia` has **no** `rpf`/`file_archive` device at all (`src/xenia/vfs/devices/` contains `disc_image_*`, `host_path_*`, `null_*` and `stfs_container_*` only), and grepping `src/xenia/vfs` and `src/xenia/xex` for a static AES key table returns nothing. So there is nothing upstream to lift the nested archive's transform from — combined with §2 of F-458 (no `RPF3` header at either nested offset, exactly one `RPF3` in the first 64 MiB), the only remaining sources for that transform are the title's own code (the guest decrypts its outer TOC, so a routine exists in-image) or content we do not have. That makes T42.8's *negative* result decision-grade rather than merely interesting. Next ID **F-463**.

### F-470 (2026-09-27 05:4x, **0 builds — pure static read of the already-generated routine, cross-checked against `w475` rows**) — **THE DISPATCH ROUTINE DELETES THE GENERATION AND NEVER LOOKS AT THE RECORD'S ID: `sub_821BC140` masks `[slot+0]` with `capacity-1` and STORES THE MASKED VALUE BACK OVER THE JOB'S OWN HANDLE at `0x821BC17C`, then reads exactly four record fields (`+4`, `+8` ×5, `+16`, `+24`) and never `+0` — so "which container am I loading" is decided by the array index alone, and F-469's six foreign records are the designed behaviour of a fast path, not a lost validity check.**

- Task:        T42.13 (#75 follow-on) — answered with no instrument
- Type:        FACT
- Class:       G (the title's own coded behaviour)
- Priority:    P0 — it tells task #15 which lever exists: the index, not the values
- Evidence:    `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.14.cpp:18850-18878` (`lwz r11,0(r26)` → `cmpwi cr6,r11,-1` → `lwz r10,24(r19)` / `addi r10,r10,-1` / `and r9,r10,r11` → **`stw r9,0(r26)`** → `lwz r10,0(r26)` / `lwz r11,52(r19)` / `mulli r10,r10,28` / `add r28,r10,r11` → `lwz r9,1540(r26)`, `cmpwi cr6,r9,0`, `beq loc_821BC53C`), with `r19 = 0x8283D190` from `lis -32124` + `addi -11888` at `:18831-18849` · field-use census over `:18805-19600`: `PPC_LOAD_U32(r28.u32 + 8)` ×5, `+ 24` ×2, `+ 16` ×2, `+ 4` ×1, **`+ 0` and `+ 12` never** · `w475.log:3451` is the one row where the mask is a no-op (`id=1`), `:41151,42789` where it costs a generation (`id=00000004/00008004` both resolving to `rec=C9E24970`)

**1. The mask is a destructive store, and that is why the generations in F-469 never line up.** The
job object's `[+0]` is overwritten with `handle & (cap-1)` *before* anything else happens, so after a
job has been entered once its handle is a bare index; two jobs whose handles differ only in
generation resolve to the **same** record address (measured in `w475`: `id=00000004` and
`id=00008004` → `rec=C9E24970` twice, and `id=00010004`/`id=00018004` → `rec=C9E24970` twice more).
So `[record+0]`'s generation tag is consumed by some *other* caller (the public handle-validation
path), and any host-side scheme whose correctness depends on the guest noticing a stale generation
cannot work — it does not look.

**2. What the routine actually consumes from a record.** Device object `[+8]` (used to call
`[dev+124]`, and again for the async read at `:18899-18904`), package offset `[+24]`, entry pointer
`[+16]`, length `[+4]`. The job's own read-list (`[slot+1540]` count, `[slot+8]/[slot+12]` =
destination/size) is the only per-job state. So a job = *its destinations* + *someone else's source*
whenever the record was re-stamped — which is 6 of 7 times in `w475` (F-469 §4).

**3. Consequence for the plan, stated as a constraint rather than a fix.** Path B cannot be "build a
record for the garage": the garage's numbers ALREADY sit in the array at two indices (F-469 §3) and
the garage's job reads a third. The two admissible levers are (i) the **index** the job resolves to —
which is `[slot+0] & 0x7FFF` read at entry, i.e. the value `sub_821BC868` wrote when it pushed, and
(ii) the **pacing**: the record at index k is only guaranteed to still describe container k for the
22-29 ms until the next push, and the consumer needs 0.08-2.7 s. Option (i) is what F-468 tried and
its failure is now explained twice over: the slot we copied INTO is one the next push re-stamps
within 22-29 ms, and at the moment we copied its `[+4]` was still 0 (F-468 §1), so we published a
zero-length record onto live queue state. Option (ii) is not a host short-circuit at all — it is the
reason `XSF-INFLATE` is 0 for all four containers, so it is the one route that can produce a *guest*
inflate. Next ID **F-471**.

### F-474 (2026-09-27 06:1x, **4 builds: `w477` probe, `w478` fence-site-only, `w479` both sites off, `w480` control after revert**) — **THE RECORD POOL'S CONTRACT IS NOW NAMED END TO END, AND MY OWN EXPLANATION OF IT IS REFUTED: the release that bumps the generation is the title's own `sub_821BD220` (`record+4 = 0`, `record+12 = old free head`, `record+0 += [0x8283D190+24]`, `free head = idx`, `ppc_recomp.14.cpp:21632-21637`), and turning OFF both of our session-72 `busy`-clearing short-circuits does not stop the re-stamping — it just makes the boot shallower (27,088 lines vs 146,068, 5 pushes vs 7, `GFx` 7 vs 13) while the job-completion callback still fires exactly once. - Task:        T42.16 (#76) answered; T42.17 (#77) the experiment, measured and REVERTED
- Type:        FACT + FIX-attempt measured and reverted + a SELF-REFUTATION of the hypothesis I formed mid-entry
- Class:       E (streamer pool/queue structure) + D (our kernel-side mitigation) + H
- Priority:    P0 — it closes the "who frees a record" question and closes one candidate cause with it
- Evidence:    pool arithmetic cross-checked against our own constants (`kTaskJoinCountAddr=0x8283D1A8` = `[0x8283D190+24]`, `kTaskJoinEntriesAddr=0x8283D1C4` = `[0x8283D190+52]`, stride 28, `src/gpu_device.cpp:4614-4621`) · release: `generated/ppc_xenon/ppc_recomp.14.cpp:21628-21637` inside `sub_821BD220` (entry `:21447`) · claim: `sub_821BCE68` (Open) writes `+16` at `:20993`, `+8/+20/+4` at `:21032-21036`, `+8 = device` / `+4 = vt[+84]` at `:21230/21241`, `+24` at `:21283/21298`, and pops the free head at `:21346-21399` · `+12` is the join wait word, which BC140's tail mutates atomically via `addi r3,r28,12; bl sub_821CE100` (`:19352-19360`) · callback tail: `ppc_recomp.14.cpp:19361-19381` reads `[slot+1540]`, and when non-zero calls `[slot+1548]` (`bctrl`, return site `0x821BC538`) — the same field F-469's `PUSH` row prints as `cb=821BC548`, which tail-branches to `sub_821C9108` → `sub_8244ED10(h,1,0)` · `build/w477.log:3441,4541,5523,6885,7915,9288,113188` = 7 `TASKJOIN-SC tag=… busy 00000001->0` rows, one per job, on the loader thread, before that job's `BC140-REC`; `build/w477.log:7677` = the ONLY `RELSEMA … lr=821BC538` row (job #1, `h=CA0F8180`, same ms as `POST-EXEC-START #1`) · `rlcAfter` (new fields on `POST-EXEC-START`, `src/gpu_device.cpp:12826-12850`) = 10/52/6/4/7/17/2 in `w477`, identical to the pre-call `RLC` in `BC140-REC` — the count-0 branch is NOT why six callbacks are missing

**1. The pool, in one paragraph.** `sub_821BD3C8` initialises it (`+0 = i`, `+4 = 0`, `+12 = i+1 or -1` at `:21789-21804`), forming the free list through `+12`. `pgStreamer::Open` pops the head at `[0x8283D190+28]`, writes the record's `+16`, `+8` (device object from `sub_821CB488`), `+4` (`vt[+84]` of that object), `+24` (`vt[+128]`/`sub_821378B8`) and `+20`. `sub_821BCB10` (F-473) validates `record+0 == handle` at enqueue. `sub_821BC140` reads `+4/+8/+16/+24` and touches only `+12` (refcount). `sub_821BD220` releases: zeroes `+4`, pushes the record back onto the free list through `+12`, and **increments `+0` by the capacity `0x8000`** — the generation. That single store answers F-469 §3 (why index *k-1* carries container *k*'s numbers with `0x8000|` set) and F-469 §5 (why generations advance outside the push path): the release is called by the loader's join, on the loader thread, at `lr=821E56B0`.

**2. My hypothesis, stated and then killed.** Because `w477` shows `TASKJOIN-SC … busy 00000001->0` firing for all seven jobs *before* those jobs dispatch, I predicted our own join-clear was the premature release that recycles records and so destroys the callbacks. record to be recycled while its job is still queued — which rehabilitates the mechanism F-474's
outcome test seemed to reject.

anything (`w479`: the boot loses 2 of 7 jobs and the callback count stays 1) because the jobs are not
completing in the first place; and keeping it is what lets the pool hand a live record to the next
container (F-469's re-stamping). So the mitigation and the recycling are two halves of one defect, and
the defect is upstream of both: **six of seven jobs never reach `sub_821BC140`'s success tail.** That,
not "the record is missing" and not "the record is wrong", is the F-186/F-187 gap restated in terms the
code now supports. Path A's feed decides whether the tail is reached (F-393's `inLeft`/`outLeft`
exits), which is the first time the two clauses of this objective sit on one measured mechanism
instead of two argued ones.

**1. Why this is the answer to the six-silent-jobs question and not another correlation.** The field is
the one the loop's own arithmetic uses to decide how much input the codec may eat, its zero value makes
that quantity non-positive, and it is non-positive *specifically* for the jobs that never reach their
tail and non-zero on every iteration for the only job that does. The re-seed condition is
`consumed == 0` (the header parse), and the silent jobs' `consumed` never returns to 0.

boundary by code we have not identified, or the descriptor block at `[sp+128]` must carry one

the `midasm_hook` route. Recorded while the pin is armed; `kF483DeferRelease` goes back to `false` in
the same commit series as the control. Next ID **F-498**.

### F-498 (2026-09-27 07:0x, **0 builds — the 20 instructions at the head of `sub_821D5E10`**) — **WHY `exp` NEVER RE-SEEDS: the header parse inside `zlibInflater::InflateBegin` is gated on `consumed == 0` (`lwz r11,8(r31); cmplwi cr6,r11,0; bne loc_821d5e7c` — `ppc_recomp.18.cpp:10850-10555` region, i.e. `if ([state+8] != 0) skip parse`), and `w496` shows the garage's `[state+8]` never returning to 0 after its first row (values `0x7FF4`/`0xFFF4` only).
